articles.summary: A secret dressing room society, Avram Grant's nickname or Neil Warnock's voicemail?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 25 Aug 2026 , · 26 mins

This week, former Manchester United, Sheffield United and Portsmouth striker Danny Webber submits three stories from his football career. Did Webber really install security cameras and fingerprint entry access to join an exclusive Sheffield United dressing room society? Did former Chelsea manager Avram Grant nickname him "World Wide Webber" after being impressed by his football knowledge? Or did Neil Warnock leave a voicemail pleading with him to ignore his reputation and sign for Sheffield United? Armed with photographs, football knowledge and plenty of suspicion, Karel and Anita investigate every claim before Webber returns to reveal the truth. articles.title: Estádio Rei Pelé: PGE identifica risco de colapso e pede interdição | G1
articles.standfirst: Laudo sobre as condições da estrutura é de junho de 2026. Recomendações foram encaminhadas a Selaj, que ficou de se manifestar sobre o caso por nota.
articles.summary: Laudo sobre as condições da estrutura é de junho de 2026. Recomendações foram encaminhadas a Selaj, que ficou de se manifestar sobre o caso por nota.
articles.body:
Estádio Rei Pelé, o Trapichão, em Maceió — Foto: Divulgação/Selaj

A Procuradoria-Geral do Estado de Alagoas (PGE-AL) identificou risco de colapso nas lajes superiores das rampas 2 e 3 do Estádio Rei Pelé, o “Trapichão” , em Maceió . A informação foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado (DOE) desta quarta-feira (26).

De acordo com o órgão, um laudo final sobre as condições da estrutura foi elaborado em junho deste ano pelo Consórcio High Tech-Progetto.

O documento foi encaminhado à Secretaria de Estado do Esporte, Lazer e Juventude de Alagoas (Selaj), responsável pelo Estádio Rei Pelé, com a recomendação de interdição parcial das rampas 2 e 3.

Segundo a 1ª Promotoria de Justiça da Capital, além da interdição, a secretaria deve adotar as seguintes medidas:

Escorar provisoriamente a estrutura das lajes;

Desocupar e interditar os alojamentos 29, 31 e 36 do Setor 5 do estádio;

Adotar as providências técnicas consideradas indispensáveis para garantir a segurança dos usuários do Rei Pelé.

O g1 procurou a Selaj, que informou que se manifestaria sobre o assunto por meio de nota. Até a publicação desta reportagem, no entanto, o documento não havia sido enviado.

A PGE também apontou outras intervenções consideradas relevantes, como a realização de correções urgentes no Setor 4 do estádio, além da recuperação e do reforço da laje da “ferradura”, no Setor 2.

A Procuradoria informou que cabe à Secretaria de Estado da Infraestrutura (Seinfra) avaliar tecnicamente essas situações, além de definir as medidas preventivas e corretivas.

Segundo o órgão, laudos anteriores não podem ser utilizados como base para avaliar os problemas identificados pelo estudo mais recente.

Por fim, a PGE recomendou que, enquanto não houver uma manifestação conclusiva que ateste a execução das medidas emergenciais e indique condições seguras para a utilização dos espaços, a Selaj impeça o acesso e o uso das áreas interditadas por qualquer pessoa.

articles.title: Cartórios de MT recebem penhora de imóveis em tempo real | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre 2020 e 2025, cerca de 1,2 mil penhoras de imóveis foram processadas em Mato Grosso. Somente nos primeiros sete meses de 2026, foram 361.
articles.summary: Entre 2020 e 2025, cerca de 1,2 mil penhoras de imóveis foram processadas em Mato Grosso. Somente nos primeiros sete meses de 2026, foram 361.
articles.body:
Os cartórios de Mato Grosso passaram a receber, em tempo real, ordens judiciais de penhora, arresto e sequestro de imóveis — Foto: 1º Serviço Notarial e Registral de Cuiabá

Os cartórios de Mato Grosso passaram a receber, em tempo real, ordens judiciais de penhora, arresto e sequestro de imóveis com a implantação do Sistema de Constrição Judicial (Constri-Jud), neste mês. A plataforma conecta os Cartórios de Registro de Imóveis de todo o país aos Tribunais de Justiça brasileiros e estabelece um fluxo eletrônico nacional para o envio dessas determinações.

A mudança busca reduzir o tempo de transmissão das ordens, diminuir retrabalho e facilitar o acompanhamento do cumprimento das decisões. De acordo com o Tribunal de Justiça de Mato Grosso (TJMT), o modelo anterior envolvia diferentes canais de comunicação, como o Penhora On-line e o Hermes Malote Digital, o que podia aumentar o tempo de tramitação e dificultar o acompanhamento das ordens.

O sistema foi desenvolvido pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema de Registro Eletrônico de Imóveis (ONR) e funciona como módulo do Sistema Eletrônico dos Registros Públicos do Judiciário (SERP-JUD), regulamentado pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ). Segundo o TJMT, o uso da ferramenta é obrigatório e padroniza a comunicação entre magistrados e cartórios .

Com o Constri-Jud, a unidade judicial insere a ordem no sistema, que é validada e autorizada pelo magistrado antes do envio eletrônico ao Registro de Imóveis competente. O registrador recebe a comunicação, realiza a análise necessária, pode apresentar eventuais exigências e informa eletronicamente o cumprimento da o

A Associação dos Notários e Registradores de Mato Grosso (Anoreg-MT) explica que o envio em tempo real ocorre a partir do momento em que o juiz expede a ordem e a disponibiliza no sistema para o Registro de Imóveis.

Isso, no entanto, não significa que a restrição seja registrada instantaneamente na matrícula. Após o recebimento da ordem pelo cartório competente, ainda são necessárias etapas obrigatórias para o cumprimento da determinação.

Segundo o TJMT, a expectativa é reduzir o intervalo entre a decisão judicial e a efetivação da restrição porque a transmissão eletrônica elimina parte dos trâmites intermediários e das comunicações manuais. O sistema também permite acompanhar as exigências e o cumprimento das ordens.

Com a nova plataforma, o envio passa a seguir um fluxo eletrônico padronizado. O sistema permite acompanhar etapas como envio, recebimento, prenotação, eventuais exigências e cumprimento da ordem. A prenotação registra a entrada do documento no cartório e estabelece a prioridade conforme a ordem de apresentação.

Sistema busca aumentar segurança em transações imobiliárias

A mudança também busca reduzir o intervalo entre a decisão judicial e a chegada da restrição ao Registro de Imóveis. Segundo a Anoreg-MT, essa redução diminui a chamada “janela de risco”, período entre a determinação da medida pela Justiça e sua chegada ao cartório.

De acordo com a associação, o envio mais rápido permite que a ordem seja apresentada ao cartório e prenotada mais rapidamente. Posteriormente, o registro da restrição na matrícula dá publicidade à medida judicial.

Para quem pretende comprar um imóvel, a mudança não altera a necessidade de verificar a situação do bem. A orientação é solicitar uma certidão atualizada da matrícula e realizar as demais verificações necessárias sobre o imóvel, os proprietários e a negociação.

“O novo sistema amplia a confiabilidade das informações que chegam ao Registro de Imóveis. Essa comunicação direta com o Judiciário reduz falhas operacionais, evita retrabalho e acelera a efetivação das restrições determinadas pela Justiça”, pontua Velenice Dias, presidente da Anoreg-MT.

Entre 2020 e 2025, cerca de 1,2 mil penhoras de imóveis foram processadas em Mato Grosso. Somente nos primeiros sete meses de 2026, foram 361.

Para a Anoreg-MT, o crescimento pode estar relacionado a fatores como a ampliação do uso de ferramentas eletrônicas pelo Judiciário, a maior localização de patrimônio imobiliário em processos de execução e o aprimoramento da integração entre a Justiça e os Registros de Imóveis.

A entidade ressalta que os números, isoladamente, não permitem afirmar que houve aumento equivalente no número de pessoas endividadas ou de processos judiciais. O volume também pode refletir maior eficiência na identificação de bens e no encaminhamento das ordens, além da conclusão de solicitações originadas anteriormente.

Nesta primeira fase, o Constri-Jud inclui ordens de penhora, arresto e sequestro de imóveis. A plataforma deverá receber posteriormente outras funcionalidades, como cancelamento de constrições, averbações premonitórias, bloqueios de matrícula e hipotecas judiciais.

Apesar da mudança no fluxo entre Justiça e cartórios, a forma de consulta da matrícula pelo cidadão não é alterada. Para uma negociação imobiliária, a recomendação é obter uma certidão atualizada e realizar as demais verificações necessárias sobre o imóvel e seus proprietários.

articles.title: Homem morto em academia em São José: vídeo mostra carro seguido | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime aconteceu na tarde desta terça-feira (25), na Zona Norte de São José dos Campos. Movimentação de suspeitos foi flagrada momentos antes dos disparos.
articles.summary: Novas imagens do CSI revelam que o homem morto em uma academia em São José dos Campos foi perseguido por suspeitos em uma moto antes dos disparos na Zona Norte.
articles.body:
Novas imagens das câmeras de monitoramento do CSI, em São José dos Campos , mostram o carro do homem de 33 anos que morreu após ser baleado em uma academia sendo seguido momentos antes de estacionar no local.

As imagens mostram o carro preto de Evandro Luiz Prudente sendo perseguido por ruas da Zona Norte por uma moto onde estavam os suspeitos do crime. Eles acompanham o veículo até a academia localizada na Avenida Rui Barbosa.

Uma outra moto também foi registrada estacionada perto da entrada principal da academia, ao lado de um ponto de ônibus.

Em seguida, as imagens mostram o atirador chegando já armado ao local e a correria de moradores, assustados com o barulho dos tiros. Na academia, outras pessoas também saem correndo.

O CSI também divulgou imagens do carro branco no qual estavam os suspeitos que foram detidos, já no estado do Rio de Janeiro, depois de abandonarem a moto, segundo a Polícia.

Evandro Luiz Prudente, de 33 anos, foi morto a tiros dentro de uma academia, na tarde desta terça-feira (25), no bairro Santana, na Zona Norte de São José dos Campos (SP).

A PM foi acionada por volta das 14h, após uma pessoa ouvir tiros e perceber várias pessoas saindo correndo da academia, localizada na Avenida Rui Barbosa.

A testemunha contou aos policiais que ouviu entre seis e dez disparos. Um vídeo de câmera de segurança (veja abaixo) mostra ao menos 14 disparos feitos contra a vítima, incluindo na cabeça.

O homem aparece sentado em uma poltrona quando é surpreendido por outro homem, que se aproxima e atira contra ele.

As imagens são fortes. Após os disparos, o suspeito deixa o local e foge acompanhado de outro indivíduo em uma motocicleta.

PM foi acionada após tiros em academia em Santana, em São José dos Campos. — Foto: Marcelo Sarlo

O Samu foi acionado e constatou a morte às 14h15. A perícia encontrou 16 estojos de munição deflagrados no local.

O caso foi registrado como homicídio no 4º Distrito Policial de São José dos Campos e é investigado pela equipe de Homicídios da DEIC.

Em nota, a Academia CompassFit lamentou o ocorrido e expressou solidariedade aos familiares da vítima.

A academia informou que está colaborando integralmente com as autoridades e permanece à disposição para auxiliar nas investigações e na apuração dos fatos. Segundo o estabelecimento, trata-se de um fato isolado e a administração não tem controle sobre ações dessa natureza.

A CompassFit informou ainda que ficará fechada nesta quarta-feira (26) e retomará as atividades na quinta-feira (27).

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3049: 14 apostas de AL acertam números, confira resultado | G1
articles.summary: Números sorteados foram: 06 - 13 - 36 - 43 - 53 - 55.
articles.body:
14 apostas de Alagoas acertaram a quadra no concurso 3049 da Mega-Sena , que teve o sorteio realizado na noite da terça-feira (25) em São Paulo. Nenhuma aposta do Brasil acertou as seis dezenas e o prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 25 milhões.

As apostas ganhadoras são das regiões Agreste, capital, Sertão, Litoral Norte e Zona da Mata de Alagoas. Todas levaram o prêmio de R$ 971,64.

Os números sorteados foram: 06 - 13 - 36 - 43 - 53 - 55.

O próximo sorteio será no quinta-feira (27).

Confira apostas ganhadoras da Mega-Sena 3049

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada.

Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Expofeira de Feira de Santana terá leilões de cavalos e bovinos | G1
articles.standfirst: 47ª Expofeira de Feira de Santana ocorrerá de 6 a 13 de setembro. Com entrada gratuita, a feira abrigará mais de mil animais.
articles.summary: 47ª Expofeira de Feira de Santana ocorrerá de 6 a 13 de setembro. Com entrada gratuita, a feira abrigará mais de mil animais.
articles.body:
Leilão da ExpoFeira — Foto: ACM | Jorge Magalhães

Dois leilões de animais estão programados para a 47ª Exposição Agropecuária de Feira de Santana (Expofeira), que será realizada entre os dias 6 e 13 de setembro, no Parque de Exposição João Martins da Silva. As vendas estão previstas para os dias 8 e 11 de setembro.

No primeiro leilão, no dia 8, serão comercializados cavalos da raça Quarto de Milha. Já no dia 11, a programação terá a venda de bovinos da raça Nelore.

Os leilões são uma tradição durante a Expofeira e reúnem criadores e compradores interessados em animais considerados de elite e com genética voltada para reprodução e melhoramento dos rebanhos.

Segundo a organização, a modalidade também permite a comercialização de lotes de animais com características semelhantes, como idade e peso, além de estabelecer condições e prazos de pagamento para os compradores.

A 47ª Expofeira de Feira de Santana acontecerá de 6 a 13 de setembro, com entrada gratuita. Considerada uma das maiores exposições agropecuárias do Nordeste, o evento terá exposições de animais e máquinas, feira de agronegócios, campeonatos, leilões e atrações ligadas à cultura regional.

Animais serão leiloados durante Expofeira em Feira de Santana — Foto: ACM | Jorge Magalhães

A programação também prevê a presença de cerca de mil animais, distribuídos entre galpões e baias. Os espaços devem receber bovinos, equinos, caprinos e ovinos.

articles.title: Prova de Vida PBH pode ser feita por biometria no app; confira | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a PBH, o procedimento agora pode ser feito por meio de biometria facial do banco e sem a necessidade de deslocamento até uma agência.
articles.summary: Segundo a PBH, o procedimento agora pode ser feito por meio de biometria facial do banco e sem a necessidade de deslocamento até uma agência.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa de um homem mexendo no celular — Foto: Freepik

Aposentados e pensionistas vinculados ao regime de previdência social da capital agora podem realizar a Prova de Vida pelo aplicativo do banco. Segundo a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte (PBH) o procedimento agora pode ser feito diretamente pelo aplicativo do Bradesco, banco conveniado ao órgão, por meio de biometria facial e sem a necessidade de deslocamento até uma agência.

Segundo a PBH, a possibilidade amplia as alternativas para os beneficiários do Regime Próprio de Previdência Social de Belo Horizonte (RPPS-BH) e traz mais comodidade e autonomia para a realização de um procedimento importante para a manutenção do benefício.

No mês de aniversário do beneficiário, o Bradesco enviará uma comunicação informando sobre a necessidade de realização da Prova de Vida. O aviso poderá aparecer no aplicativo por meio de notificação push, janela de aviso ou card disponível no perfil.

Para realizar o procedimento, o beneficiário deverá acessar o App Bradesco, selecionar “Conta”, entrar em “Perfil” e clicar no Card de Prova de Vida , disponível durante o período de convocação.

Em seguida, o usuário deve seguir as orientações apresentadas pelo aplicativo para realizar a captura da biometria facial. Após a captura, o sistema fará a validação da identidade. Todo o procedimento pode ser realizado pelo celular, sem necessidade de comparecimento a uma agência.

A opção também está disponível para beneficiários que possuem portabilidade de salário, desde que tenham acesso ao aplicativo Bradesco.

A nova opção utiliza a tecnologia de biometria facial já disponível no banco e permite que o beneficiário faça a confirmação de sua identidade de forma digital, rápida e segura, utilizando o próprio celular.

Pensionistas menores de 18 anos de idade, beneficiários impedidos de se locomover por questões médicas, declarados absolutamente incapazes em processo judicial ou que residem ou estejam temporariamente no exterior possuem procedimentos específicos.

Nessas situações, é necessário acessar o Portal da PBH, clicar em “Acesso Rápido” e, em seguida, em “Prova de Vida” para consultar as orientações.

articles.title: Canetas emagrecedoras em crianças: SBP alerta para riscos à saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria alerta para possíveis impactos no crescimento, perda de massa muscular e risco de transtornos alimentares; entidade recomenda acompanhamento médico.
articles.summary: A Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria alerta que canetas emagrecedoras em crianças podem causar perda de massa muscular, transtornos alimentares e afetar o crescimento.
articles.body:
A Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria (SBP) lançou um alerta sobre o uso de canetas emagrecedoras por crianças e adolescentes . Segundo a entidade, os medicamentos podem trazer riscos à saúde e afetar o desenvolvimento físico de pessoas que ainda estão em fase de crescimento .

O alerta ocorre após vídeos de mães aplicando os medicamentos nos filhos circularem nas redes sociais (veja no vídeo acima) . Em uma das gravações, uma mãe afirma que aplica o medicamento na filha de 17 anos por indicação médica. Em outra publicação, uma mulher diz que levou a filha, de 11 anos e 70 kg, ao médico e recebeu recomendação para o uso da tirzepatida.

As postagens também recebem comentários de adolescentes interessados em usar os medicamentos. Em um deles, um usuário do TikTok afirma ter 13 anos, 79 kg e 1,70 metro de altura e pergunta se pode fazer o tratamento .

Brasil já registra 7 milhões de crianças e adolescentes obesos. — Foto: Reprodução/Bom Dia Brasil

Segundo a Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria, o uso das canetas pode diminuir a ingestão de proteínas e minerais importantes para o desenvolvimento.

"Ele vai diminuir a ingestão de proteínas e de minerais que vão afetar o seu crescimento, principalmente o estirão do crescimento do adolescente", alerta Crésio Alves, presidente do Departamento Científico de Endocrinologia da SBP.

Outro possível efeito é a diminuição e a perda de massa muscular. "Um segundo efeito adverso nessa faixa etária é a diminuição e perda de massa muscular", continua.

Além disso, o médico também alerta para o risco de que o uso das canetas seja um gatilho para transtornos alimentares, como anorexia nervosa e bulimia nervosa.

Canetas emagrecedoras com venda ilegal no Brasil também são buscadas por pais de crianças e adolescentes. — Foto: Reprodução/Bom Dia Brasil

"Terceiro efeito adverso, pode ser um gatilho para transtornos alimentares, como anorexia nervosa e bulimia nervosa, que são condições difíceis de você tratar uma vez instaladas", diz.

O Brasil tem mais de 17 milhões de crianças e adolescentes entre 5 e 19 anos com excesso de peso , segundo o Atlas Mundial da Obesidade. Desse total, 7 milhões já são considerados obesos .

O uso de canetas emagrecedoras, porém, deve ser acompanhado por profissionais de saúde. Entre os possíveis problemas associados ao uso estão pancreatite, que é a inflamação do pâncreas; hipoglicemia, caracterizada pela redução da quantidade de açúcar no sangue; e cálculos na vesícula.

Riscos para crianças e adolescentes, segundo a SBP. — Foto: Reprodução/Bom Dia Brasil

Canetas compradas no exterior também preocupam

Outro risco apontado pela Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria é o uso de produtos comprados fora do Brasil.

Em uma das publicações, uma mãe afirma que pretende comprar uma caneta para o filho de 12 anos, que pesa 93 kg, no Paraguai. A caneta citada na reportagem é uma marca cuja venda é proibida no Brasil.

A SBP alerta que não é possível saber com segurança o que há no produto ou qual é a quantidade da substância presente.

"É um perigo porque a gente não sabe o que tem exatamente dentro daquela caneta. A gente não sabe a quantidade, a gente não tem certeza se aquilo é puro, se está contaminado ou não", afirma amédica Maria Edna de Melo, endocrinologista da Associação Brasileira para o Estudo da Obesidade e Síndrome Metabólica (Abeso).

"Então, tanto a eficácia quanto os efeitos colaterais, eles são imprevisíveis", completa.

A entidade também chama atenção para a pressão estética sobre crianças e adolescentes, que ainda estão desenvolvendo a autoestima e o comportamento.

Segundo a SBP, esse público não deve simplesmente usar as canetas para perder peso rapidamente, atingir padrões estéticos ou compensar o sedentarismo. A recomendação é que o tratamento seja feito com acompanhamento médico.

As canetas emagrecedoras autorizadas pela Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) precisam de receita médica. A prescrição fica retida na farmácia no momento da compra.

articles.title: Harpia é flagrada predando macaco-guariba em área remota da Amazônia | G1
articles.standfirst: Flagrante aconteceu por acaso durante expedição de campo; câmera trap foi deixada junto a presa na tentativa de registrar o retorno do predador.
articles.summary: Flagrante aconteceu por acaso durante expedição de campo; câmera trap foi deixada junto a presa na tentativa de registrar o retorno do predador.
articles.body:
Uma harpia foi flagrada predando um macaco-guariba (também chamado de bugio) durante uma expedição em uma área remota da Amazônia paraense. O momento foi registrado pelo biólogo Will Pessoa, que avistou o animal por acaso enquanto retornava de um ponto de pesquisa para outro, na estrada, por volta das 10h.

"Eu vi um movimento no meio da estrada, tava com vegetação, não consegui entender o que que era. Quando eu fui me aproximando, eu vi que era uma ave, e aí na hora que eu identifiquei, o bicho saiu voando", contou o biólogo. Foi então que a equipe percebeu se tratar de uma harpia.

Veja mais notícias do Terra da Gente, no g1:

Ao se aproximar, o biólogo constatou que a ave havia deixado a presa, o macaco-guariba, caída no chão, enquanto circulava entre as árvores próximas .

"A gente percebeu que ela deixou a presa no chão, o macaco guariba ficou lá no chão, e o animal ficou circulando, pulando, saindo de uma árvore para outra, enquanto a gente tava fazendo o registro", relatou Pessoa.

Harpia é flagrada predando macaco-guariba em área remota da Amazônia paraense — Foto: Will Pessoa

Diante da cena, a equipe teve a ideia de instalar uma câmera trap, equipamento equipado com sensor de presença que aciona a gravação de vídeo ou foto automaticamente, próximo ao corpo do macaco. A aposta partiu de um comportamento já conhecido de aves de rapina.

"A gente sabe que geralmente águia, gavião, falcão, ele quando deixa uma presa cair ou por algum motivo ele deixa lá, ele volta para pegar", explicou o biólogo.

O equipamento foi configurado para gravar vídeo com som e com sensibilidade de sensor aumentada, de forma a captar qualquer movimento no local.

"Coloquei essa câmera próximo ao macaco e deixei lá, na torcida de que esse animal voltasse para pegar a sua comida, já que ele não conseguiu terminar seu lanche", disse Pessoa.

No dia seguinte, a equipe retornou ao ponto para verificar o resultado. "Passei lá super ansioso para tentar ver se esse bicho tinha pegado o macaco.

Chegamos lá, o macaco não estava, alguém levou. Pode ter sido a harpia ou pode ter sido algum outro animal de chão", relatou o biólogo, que adiantou ainda ter conseguido registrar, com a câmera trap, o momento em que a harpia retorna ao local para buscar a presa.

Para Will Pessoa, flagrantes como esse têm valor direto para a conservação da espécie, classificada como ameaçada.

"Registro de predação, da sua biologia, da sua ecologia são fundamentais para compreensão de como esse bicho vive, como é sua dieta, em que horários de atividade eles estão, e tudo isso a gente usa para trabalhos de conservação das espécies", afirmou.

O biólogo reforça ainda o papel de registros feitos por pesquisadores e por qualquer pessoa que cruze com o animal na natureza. "Isso aqui, um registro seja nosso, seja de qualquer pessoa, ele é muito útil e é muito importante para que a gente compreenda como é a dinâmica populacional, a ecologia, a biologia desses animais", concluiu.

articles.title: Três meses após ser encontrado morto na Argentina, viúva recebe corpo de paranaense que desapareceu enquanto ela fazia compras no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Sumiço de Antônio Rodrigues Júnior, de 46 anos, foi em maio, enquanto ele esperava a esposa voltar de Cidade do Leste. Corpo foi liberado após exame de DNA.
articles.summary: Antônio Rodrigues Júnior teve a identidade confirmada por DNA após desaparecer em Foz do Iguaçu e ser localizado no Rio Paraná, em território argentino.
articles.body:
Após três meses de espera, a família de Antônio Rodrigues Júnior, de 46 anos, finalmente recebeu o corpo do paranaense e pôde se despedir dele.

Morador de Céu Azul , no Oeste do Paraná, Antônio desapareceu em maio, em Foz do Iguaçu , enquanto aguardava a esposa fazer compras em Cidade do Leste, no Paraguai.

O corpo foi encontrado seis dias depois , em 16 de maio, no Rio Paraná, na região de Porto Leoni, na província de Misiones, na Argentina. Desde então, a família aguardava a confirmação da identidade e a liberação para o traslado ao Brasil.

Segundo a viúva, Adriane, o exame de DNA confirmou a identidade de Antônio. A família havia reconhecido o corpo pelas roupas e por um anel que ele usava no dia do desaparecimento.

“Foi bem difícil. A gente tinha esperança de que saísse mais rápido, porque nós tínhamos certeza que era ele e a gente queria que não fosse, na verdade. Foi bastante sofrimento”, contou Adriane.

Antônio Rodrigues Junior, tem 46 anos, e desapareceu enquanto esperava a esposa fazer compras no Paraguai. — Foto: Cedida/Adriane Paulo de Miranda

A viúva também falou sobre o impacto da morte para a filha do casal, que é menor de idade.

“Ele tem filha pequena, de menor, e até ela entender e tudo, nós passamos por bastante sofrimento.”

articles.summary: MUMBAI: FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Tuesday declared that a statewide compliance order on the ban on loose edible oil was non-negotiable and th.
articles.body: MUMBAI: FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on Tuesday declared that a statewide compliance order on the ban on loose edible oil was non-negotiable and the food safety regulator said accepting the demands to relax or cancel would be inappropriate, but the administration did a U-turn an hour later and withdrew the statements.An official said a meeting is scheduled with govt to discuss standard operating procedures and a decision will be made after that.TOI had earlier reported that FDA's ban on the sale of loose edible oil had come up for discussion at a cabinet meeting on Monday. CM Devendra Fadnavis had stressed that govt is seeking a "middle path". "Strict quality needs to be maintained, but at the same time, traditional businesses also need to be protected," he had said.There was also a letter sent to FDA by Edible Oil Merchants Association.Before making a U-turn, FDA said in a statement, "They (retailers) were informed on Aug 18 that their demands to relax or cancel the rules... are not consistent with existing legal and regulatory provisions." It said accepting such demands "would not be appropriate from the perspective of food safety and public health".Mundhe said the prohibition on the sale of loose or unpackaged edible oil is not a newly introduced decision. "This provision has been applicable across the country since 2011, and the administration has issued a statewide compliance order to ensure effective and uniform implementation of the existing law, which must be strictly obeyed." These, too, were withdrawn.The administration provided the examples of Delhi, UP and Tamil Nadu, where such bans are in place. It said Maharashtra had granted temporary and time-bound exemptions or extensions on the sale of loose edible oil from time to time. "This extension was limited up to 2020 and was not a permanent permission," it said.Meanwhile, FDA suspended the license of Ayub's Restaurant in Fort last Saturday over improper storage of food items like eggs at room temperature, failure to segregate and store raw and cooked food, presence of houseflies, and lack of pest control.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Thameslink to replace over 60,000 'ironing board' train seats
articles.summary: Greater Thameslink Railway says these upgrades are part of the wider renationalisation plans.
articles.body:
"Ironing board" seats on some commuter trains will get extra cushioning, the transport secretary has said, more than a decade after the government spent £1.6bn of public money building the fleet.

Heidi Alexander announced that more than 60,000 seats on all 115 Thameslink trains would get new cushions and backrests, replacing much-criticised thin and hard seats.

She said the work, set to begin in 2027 and last two years, was "public ownership of our railways in action" as part of the new Great British Railways programme.

However, some have criticised how the Department for Transport (DfT) awarded a £1.6bn contract for the trains despite being warned of the seat discomfort at the time.

The seat upgrades are part of wider improvements planned for the Thameslink network after Greater Thameslink Railway came into public ownership in May 2026 .

Other measures included an increase in Gatwick Express services from December and a programme to refurbish train toilets and remove graffiti across the fleet.

Alexander said: "We'll start getting rid of the dreaded 'ironing board seats' so passengers can enjoy comfier, more pleasant journeys on some of Britain's busiest commuter routes."

She said wider rail reforms would continue under the planned Great British Railways organisation, which is intended to oversee rail services across England.

The class-700 Thameslink trains were heralded by the DfT as "state-of-the-art" and "a fantastic deal" for taxpayers when they were rolled out between 2016 and 2019.

That followed the DfT spending £1.6bn of taxpayers' money for German manufacturer Siemens to build the trains in 2013, following a bidding process which began in 2008.

DfT's own procurement guidance document for the fleet, seen by the BBC, stressed that they should be "high capacity" and "reduced weight".

It said the new electric fleet would have a design that "must cater for [about] 1,000 people to board or alight at one time" and a "2+2 seat layout to ease flow and provide standing space".

Some have claimed that this aim to maximise capacity and standing space for commuters led to the seats being so thinly cushioned.

Responding to Alexander's post on X praising the new re-cushioning project, Graeme Pickering, senior correspondent at Railway Magazine, wrote: "Might have been wise not to frame this as 'public ownership fixes private sector mess' when it was the DfT which procured said trains."

Two years before the Thameslink trains were rolled out to the public, a prototype was unveiled at London's Excel centre in 2014.

A panel of volunteer experts at Railfuture, the UK's leading independent rail passenger campaign group, went to have a look and was not impressed.

In a report, they warned: "We found the seats very hard and imagine this will soon lead to complaints from passengers, particularly bearing in mind that some journeys on these trains will be up to 130 miles long such as Peterborough or Cambridge or Bedford to Gatwick & Brighton and taking over two hours."

Passenger comfort was "severely compromised" and "we strongly urge reconsideration of the design before series production takes place", their report warned.

Production went ahead without the seats being redesigned. The DfT argues that it was not possible to renegotiate a private sector contract until public ownership took effect earlier this year.

The BBC understands more details will be released in the autumn on the contract negotiations for the new cushions.

John Whitehurst, chief executive of GTR, said passenger feedback had played a key role in shaping the plans.

"Our customers told us that comfort matters, which was why we'd been working on plans to improve seating on Thameslink services," he said.

Thameslink operates services across the South East, including Sussex, Surrey and some areas of Kent.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has taken into custody a man wanted in connection with the alleged murder of his former girlfriend in the United States after non-bailable warrants issued against him were executed, according to a court order passed on August 25.Additional chief judicial magistrate Animesh Bhaskar Mani Tripathi recorded that the accused, Arjun Sharma, was arrested after the warrants were executed and directed that he be taken into custody and that necessary custody warrants be prepared, news agency ANI reported.The accused was medically examined following his arrest, with no injuries reported. The arresting officer also informed his family about the arrest, the order said.The development comes in connection with the alleged killing of 27-year-old Telugu woman Nikitha Godishala in Columbia, Howard County, Maryland.Nikitha was allegedly killed around New Yearâs Eve in 2025.According to US police allegations, Sharma, who was Nikithaâs former boyfriend, allegedly stabbed her, reported her missing and subsequently fled the US for India.Nikithaâs body was later allegedly found inside a suitcase kept in a closet at Sharmaâs apartment during a police search. US authorities believe she was killed between December 31, 2025 and January 2, 2026, while Sharma allegedly left the US on January 3.Sharma is facing two counts of murder and two counts of assault before the District Court of Maryland for Howard County.The charges carry a punishment of more than one year in prison and correspond to offences under Sections 101 and 118 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Delhi court order said.CBI flags Hyderabad caseDuring the hearing, the CBI informed the court that Sharma was also a suspect in an FIR registered at Lallaguda Police Station in Hyderabad.The court was told that a Lallaguda police officer had served a notice at Sharmaâs address in Agra. A daily diary entry was subsequently made before a raid was conducted to execute the non-bailable warrants.Special public prosecutor Naveen Kumar Matta appeared for the Union of India along with advocates Md Faizan and Rohit Singh Bora, while advocate Ajay Sharma represented the accused.Extradition proceedings underwayThe proceedings in India stem from an extradition request made under the India-US Extradition Treaty, notified on September 14, 1999.The court record said the extradition petition was supported by authenticated documents, including the arrest warrant issued by US authorities. It also recorded that the requirements under Article 2 of the treaty had been met.US authorities had launched an international manhunt for Sharma after Nikithaâs body was allegedly recovered from his apartment.A US arrest warrant was subsequently issued against him on first- and second-degree murder charges.Nikithaâs father had earlier alleged that a monetary dispute between his daughter and Sharma preceded the alleged killing.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Cash buyers dominated the US housing boom. Now financed buyers are fighting back
articles.summary: News News: Cash is losing some of its advantage in the US housing market as home sales slow, inventory increases and price growth moderates, giving buyers relyin.
articles.body: Cash is losing some of its advantage in the US housing market as home sales slow, inventory increases and price growth moderates, giving buyers relying on mortgages a better chance of competing.The share of homes bought with cash fell to 31.4% in the first four months of 2026, from 32.3% during the same period a year earlier, according to Realtor.com data cited by CNBC.Cash purchases have also declined faster than the overall housing market. Total home sales fell 8.5% year-on-year during the period, while the number of cash sales dropped 11.2%.The shift comes as price growth has slowed sharply. The national median home price increased just 0.2% annually, compared with 1.8% growth in 2025 and a peak annual increase of 15.4% in 2021.âCash buyers arenât disappearing; theyâre simply becoming less dominant as the housing market finds its footing,â Hannah Jones, senior economist at Realtor.com, said in a release.âMore inventory and moderating prices are giving financed buyers more opportunities to compete,â she said, adding that cash continues to give sellers confidence that transactions can close quickly and with fewer surprises.Cash buyers lose ground after years of dominanceCash had gained importance during the pandemic-era housing boom, when limited supply and intense bidding wars made cash offers particularly attractive. Its importance continued after interest rates rose.But recent data indicate that trend is reversing.According to a National Association of Realtors survey cited by CNBC, cash accounted for 26% of existing-home sales in July 2026, down from 31% in July 2025.The decline has not been uniform across the country. Pittsburgh, Austin and San Francisco recorded increases in the share of transactions completed with cash compared with a year earlier.In those markets, the rise was also accompanied by an increase in the actual number of cash purchases.Financed buyers are winning competitive dealsDana Bull, a real estate agent in the Boston area, said she has seen fewer cash buyers even though the Boston market remains competitive.âThere was certainly a period of time when cash was king, which was right after interest rates climbed and aggressive bidding wars were commonplace. Itâs been tapering off,â Bull said, as quoted by CNBC.She said buyers are still waiving financing terms in some cases, while she recommends that clients in hotter neighbourhoods obtain pre-underwriting, rather than only pre-approval, to strengthen their offers against cash buyers.Bull cited two recent examples in which financed buyers won competitive bidding situations.âI had a client win a bidding war against about 15 offers this spring (financed with pre-underwriting), and my team member just beat out 27 other offers on a house in Arlington (also financed),â she said.âI donât think this would have happened in 2022-2025 during the cash craze,â Bull added.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Mumbai builder told to pay Rs 6 crore to housing society over 20-year delay in occupation certificate
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has directed a Mumbai builder to pay Rs 6 crore to a cooperative housing societ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has directed a Mumbai builder to pay Rs 6 crore to a cooperative housing society after finding that its members had been living under the continuing risk of demolition for more than 20 years because the developer failed to obtain an occupation certificate.The commission also directed the builder to obtain the occupation certificate within 12 months and pay Rs 10 lakh towards litigation costs. The judgment was pronounced on August 17, 2026.What was the dispute over the housing society's redevelopment?As per the commission order, Tirupati Devi Cooperative Housing Society, comprising 33 members occupying 25 flats in two wings of Balaji Apartments in Santa Cruz, had entered into a redevelopment agreement with Raja Construction Company on March 14, 2005. Under the agreement, the developer was required to demolish the old buildings, construct new ones and provide flats to the existing members. The developer was also responsible for obtaining the occupation certificate and new water connection.The developer handed over possession of the flats from 2008 onwards. However, the society alleged that it failed to provide the sanctioned building plans, occupation certificate, completion certificate and new water connections.After an RTI application, the members allegedly came to know that the construction did not match the sanctioned plans. The society further alleged that additional construction had been carried out and because of the same the authority denied granting the occupation certificate.The society approached the NCDRC in 2013 seeking compensation for the delay, differences in the flat areas, regularisation charges and the failure to provide the required certificates. However, the builder denied the allegations and argued that the complaint was filed late. It also claimed that some of the flat owners had themselves made illegal changes to their flats and because of that the the occupation certificate was not issued.The commission, however, found that there was no evidence supporting the builder's claim that the members had carried out illegal construction. It noted that the developer had itself agreed to provide the additional carpet area and had undertaken responsibility for obtaining the occupation certificate and completing the necessary formalities.What did the commission say while holding the builder responsible?The bench comprising President A.P. Sahi and member Bharatkumar Pandya, noted that although the members had received possession of their flats in 2008, the legality of the construction remained in doubt because the construction was in excess of or contrary to the approved plans. It also found that the developer had taken the risk of constructing additional area and had failed to obtain the required approvals.âThough the possession is being enjoyed by the members from 2008 onwards, the legality of the extent of construction and of such possession is in jeopardy in view of the refusal or resistance by the authorities to grant such permission in view of the fact of part of the construction being in excess of or contrary to the approved plan as submitted by the Developer to the authorities,â the commission said.The commission further rejected the builder's argument that the society members were responsible for the problem. It said the developer had the responsibility of preparing proper plans, carrying out construction according to those plans and obtaining the occupation certificate.âThere is no evidence on record and no merit in the contention of the OP that the members have made any illegal construction in their units. It is the OP who promised, constructed and handed over the flats with 20 percent additional carpet area to the original members,â it further added.The commission held that the absence of the occupation certificate had become a continuing problem for the society and its members. It noted that they had been facing anxiety and the risk of demolition for more than 20 years.âIn our considered opinion, the non-obtaining of the OC and putting the members under the continuing risk of demolition of the building due to illegality in construction over a longish period of more than 20 years, calls for the compensation at enhanced 1.5 times the stipulated rate, which would be just and fair and would duly take care of the anxiety and mental agony and adversity faced and being faced by the society and its members,â the bench noted.The commission noted that the redevelopment agreement itself provided for compensation of Rs 1 lakh per month if the developer failed to complete the project within 24 months. However, considering the long delay and the continuing risk faced by the members, it increased the compensation rate to 1.5 times that amount for the period from June 2008 to August 2026. This worked out to Rs 3.24 crore, after which the commission added another Rs 26 lakh for the additional hardship and expenses caused by the absence of municipal water connection and additional municipal taxes.The commission then awarded a further Rs 2.5 crore, taking the total compensation to Rs 6 crore. It said the members had been living under a continuing threat of demolition because the occupation certificate had still not been obtained.The builder and its partners were held jointly and severally responsible for the deficiency in service. The commission directed them to pay the Rs 6 crore compensation within three months. If they failed to pay, the amount would carry 8 percent simple interest until full payment.The commission also directed the builder to pay all necessary charges and obtain the occupation certificate within 12 months, and hand it over to the society and its 33 current members. It further directed the builder to pay Rs 10 lakh towards litigation costs within three months.

articles.title: Indian-origin former Optum director sentenced to 3 years in prison over $950,000 fraud scheme
articles.summary: US News: Karan Gupta, an Indian-origin former director at Optum, has been sentenced to three years in prison for a $950,000 fraud scheme involving no-show jobs and kickbacks. Gupta's actions impacted a healthcare provider serving millions of Americans.
articles.body: An Indian-origin former director at healthcare company Optum has been sentenced to three years in prison for his role in a scheme that defrauded the company of more than $950,000.Karan Gupta, 48, based in California, was sentenced on August 24 after being convicted of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, 10 counts of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering,according to the US Attorney's Office for Minnesota.Gupta, who served as a senior director at Optum, was found guilty by a federal jury on February 17 following a six-day trial.According to court documents, Gupta arranged a no-show job for his longtime friend, Shangraf Kaul, 45, of East Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania.Gupta hired Kaul as a data engineering manager on his team in late 2015, despite Kaul allegedly lacking the qualifications for the position. Prosecutors said Kaul performed no work at Optum for more than three years while receiving a six-figure salary.Gupta allegedly demanded that Kaul return about 60% of his salary as kickbacks. The payments were initially made through cash deposits into Gupta's bank account before the pair used a separate checking account that Gupta could access to conceal the money transfers.The scheme was uncovered after Optum terminated Gupta in November 2019 over his involvement in a similar no-show employee fraud. The company investigated the matter and referred it to federal law enforcement.US Attorney Daniel N. Rosen said the fraud affected more than just the company.âDefrauding a private company is not a victimless crime,â Rosen said, adding that Gupta's actions undermined a healthcare provider relied upon by millions of Americans.Gupta's co-conspirator, Kaul, pleaded guilty in February 2025 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Startup Bets on Aluminum as Cleaner Fuel to Power Data Centers
articles.summary: A California startup has raised $35 million to develop a system that turns scrap aluminum into a backup power source for data centers. The goal: to create a...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A California startup has raised $35 million to develop a system that turns scrap aluminum into a backup power source for data centers. The goal: to create a cleaner alternative to burning diesel.

Voya Energy's financing round was led by Energy Impact Partners LP and included billionaire venture capitalist John Doerr, Mantis VC, StepStone, Founders Fund, Overmatch Ventures and Seven Stars, the firm said Wednesday in an emailed statement. Voya plans to use the money to build generators that use aluminum-based fuel for testing at sites by the end of 2027.

Chief Executive Officer Richard Wang said the system ultimately aims to compete with diesel generators, a standard backup power source at data centers that helps keep equipment running during grid outages. Unlike burning diesel, which causes air pollution, Voya's system uses an electrochemical reaction to release energy from aluminum, with zero carbon emissions.

The firm is betting that data center developers who face increasing scrutiny for their environmental impacts will pay for a diesel alternative that Voya said is quieter, takes up less space and is cleaner than burning fossil fuels.

"The local air pollution of these generators is one of the reasons why there's a big data center backlash right now," said Shayle Kann of Energy Impact Partners, who helped conceive the idea and build Voya with Wang and his co-founders.

Voya's generator design involves feeding recycled aluminum into a chemical solution, triggering an electrochemical reaction that releases energy. The company has an in-house prototype of the technology, which hasn't been proven at a commercial scale.

Nearly a dozen companies including data centers, utilities and industrial manufacturers have partnered with Voya for near-term pilot demonstrations, the firm said, though Wang declined to name them.

Voya's aluminum-focused system is being developed during a period of soaring prices for the lightweight metal. US prices have surged in the past 18 months due to import tariffs from the Trump administration, tightening inventories and supply disruptions from conflicts in the Middle East, a significant producing region. That has helped drive up demand and prices for recycled aluminum.

articles.title: Trump's Canada auto tariffs could end up denting US GDP: Oxford Economics
articles.summary: President Trump's threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, and car parts and ensuing trade war could hit an already weakened US economy, warns a new...
articles.body:
President Trump's threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, and car parts and the ensuing trade war could hit an already weakened US economy, warns a new report from Oxford Economics.

Oxford Economics said it will revise its US tariff assumptions higher in its September baseline forecast to reflect a breakdown in US-Canada trade talks over the weekend. The 50% Section 338 tariffs unveiled in July on select Canadian goods have come into effect , nudging the overall US effective tariff rate up 0.2 percentage points to 9.9%.

In addition, Trump has threatened to slap 50% duties on Canadian vehicles and parts starting Jan. 1, 2027, a move that could push the overall US effective tariff rate to either 10.1% or 10.4%, depending on whether exemptions for USMCA compliance are granted.

Canada vowed to match the duties "dollar for dollar" and just announced tariffs as high as 50% on hundreds of American products . This tit-for-tat escalation alone is poised to trim 0.1 percentage point off US GDP growth next year, the firm said.

"The impact of the Canadian auto tariffs on the US economy would be a rounding error, but this doesn't account for any retaliation by Canada, which would amplify the drag on US growth," Oxford's US economist Bernard Yaros wrote in the report.

Yaros added that the auto duties would disproportionately hurt Midwestern states with large auto sectors that lean on Canadian-made components, mainly Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana. Michigan alone accounts for approximately 22% of US imports of intermediate automotive goods from Canada.

For now, car buyers have largely been spared the tariff expense. New-vehicle prices are only about 0.4% higher than their pre-tariff trend, Oxford Economics estimates, as automakers and dealers absorbed most of the earlier tariff costs.

Had those costs fully passed through, auto prices today would be nearly 5% above their pre-tariff baseline, with core goods inflation running 0.4 percentage points higher and core inflation up 0.1 point.

While automaker profit margins took a sharp hit starting in the second quarter of 2025, refunds from the Supreme Court's invalidation of Trump's broad tariffs led to GM ( GM ) and Ford ( F ) boosting their 2026 profit outlooks.

But further tariff pain will reverse those effects. Honda said on Tuesday that it will reconsider US investment in a new plant if a proper USMCA deal is not ratified.

"If the US imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, the inflationary fallout is unlikely to be benign," Yaros noted, warning that thinning margins could push more costs on to consumers and drive buyers toward the used car market.

articles.title: Middlesbrough murder investigation as two people die in house fire
articles.summary: Cleveland Police says it "cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime" after the fire near Middlesbrough.
articles.body:
A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire.

The blaze in Grangetown, Middlesbrough, broke out just before 05:30 BST and also left a woman in hospital in a critical condition, alongside a further three people who suffered non-life threatening injuries.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating what had happened but was "keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time".

The fire happened about two miles from the A66 crash that killed five young men and two police officers on Saturday morning.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander Supt Emily Harrison said the force was working to "establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened".

"We will have a high visibility presence in the Grangetown area as this investigation progresses, and to provide reassurance to local communities, who will no doubt be impacted by this tragic incident."

Patrols have been increased in the local area to "reassure the local community", the force said.

Firefighters damped down the smoking roof of the home which has been wrecked by the fire.

A ladder was propped against a rear upstairs window of the family home.

A neighbour, who asked not to be named, said: "My daughter heard shouting and screaming this morning.

The neighbour said a family lived at the house, adding: "I don't know the people who live there, we just say hello when we walk past."

Police officers guarded a cordon around the scene and Northern Powergrid staff were also on site.

Cleveland Fire Brigade said it sent six fire engines and the Incident Command Unit to the scene.

A spokesperson said road closures were in place in the surrounding area and asked members of the public to avoid the area where possible.

Redcar MP Anna Turley said the community had faced a "profound amount of heartbreak over the past few weeks".

She said: "I am devastated to hear of the tragic loss of life following this morning's fire in Grangetown.

"My deepest condolences are with the families, friends and loved ones of those who have died, and my thoughts are also with those injured and receiving treatment."

Grangetown councillor Adam Brook urged people not to speculate.

He said: "Many residents have been in touch with me throughout the morning, and I know there is understandably a great deal of concern.

"However, I would urge people not to speculate or share unconfirmed information."

The families of the people involved have been informed and they are being supported by specialist officers.

articles.title: In the 1970s, Britain imported North American signal crayfish for farms; they escaped, bred in huge numbers and now infest rivers across England, Wales and Scotland, carrying a plague deadly to native crayfish
articles.summary: UK News: In the 1970s, British aquaculture businesses imported North American signal crayfish to stock farms, hoping to build a profitable new freshwater fishe.
articles.body: In the 1970s, British aquaculture businesses imported North American signal crayfish to stock farms, hoping to build a profitable new freshwater fishery. But the plan backfired: the hardy invaders escaped into rivers, multiplied rapidly and spread across England, Wales and Scotland. Today they dominate many waterways and carry crayfish plague, a disease that is usually fatal to the UKâs only native crayfish, the white-clawed species. The UK Government documents describe signal crayfish as a textbook case of how non-native species can damage biodiversity, out-compete natives and alter river ecosystems. This story is based on UK government policy reports and recent Environment Agency reporting on native crayfish conservation. Read on to know more:How signal crayfish arrived, and why they spread so fastSignal crayfish (Pacifastacus leniusculus) were brought into the UK from North America in the 1970s for farming, intended as a commercial species for restaurants and local markets. They are larger, faster-growing and more aggressive than the native white-clawed crayfish (Austropotamobius pallipes), giving them an immediate advantage in competition for food and shelter.Once they escaped from farms into the wild, they proved exceptionally good at colonising new habitats. They breed in large numbers, tolerate a wide range of water conditions and can move through connected river systems with relative ease. Over the decades, they have established populations in rivers and streams across much of England, Wales and Scotland, turning what began as a controlled aquaculture experiment into a widespread invasive-species problem.The hidden weapon: crayfish plagueThe most damaging aspect of the signal crayfish invasion is not just competition: itâs disease. Signal crayfish carry crayfish plague, a waterborne pathogen caused by the oomycete Aphanomyces astaci. The disease rarely harms signal crayfish themselves, but it is usually lethal to white-clawed crayfish, which have no natural immunity.When signal crayfish move into a river system that holds native populations, they can trigger mass die-offs.The plague spreads through the water and via contaminated equipment, clothing and boats, making it hard to contain once established. This dynamic has pushed the white-clawed crayfish toward local extinctions in many catchments and contributed to its status as an endangered species in the UK.Impact on rivers, banks and other wildlifeSignal crayfish do far more than crowd out native species; they tear apart whole river ecosystems. As they dig burrows into riverbanks, they weaken the soil and trigger severe erosion in small streams and ditches. Their relentless appetite makes things worse. By devouring fish eggs and aquatic bugs, they starve local wildlife and unravel complex food webs. Once these aggressive generalists take over, rich, diverse waters degrade into simplified systems dominated by a single pest. Protecting our native crayfish is about more than saving one creature. It is about keeping entire freshwater habitats healthy and resilient.A recent scare and glimmers of hope for native crayfishThe vulnerability of native populations was underscored in autumn 2024 when some 100 white-clawed crayfish were found dead in the River Wansbeck catchment in Northumberland, a nationally important stronghold for the species. Surveys in summer 2025 revealed that many affected crayfish had unusual orange patches and ulcers on their shells, but the symptoms didnât appear to be fatal at the population level. Investigations by the Environment Agency, the National Trust and university researchers found that some crayfish, especially younger individuals, could recover through normal moulting, and that mortality seemed concentrated in older, larger animals. No further deaths were reported after autumn 2024, and the Wansbeck population is still considered a key refuge for the species. Importantly, no signal crayfish are known from the Wansbeck catchment, and crayfish plague was ruled out as the cause of those particular mortalities.What the government is doing, and what the public can doUK policy explicitly recognises signal crayfish as a non-native species that has âcaused troubleâ for native wildlife, and uses it as a case study for why stricter controls on importing and moving live aquatic species are necessary.Regulations now require risk assessments for new species introductions and govern the movement of live fish and crayfish between water bodies to reduce disease spread.Conservation efforts focus on creating âark sitesâ, isolated water bodies where white-clawed crayfish can live and breed without exposure to signal crayfish or plague. After the 2024 incident, healthy âberriedâ females were rescued from the Wansbeck, their eggs hatched in captivity, and the offspring are being released into ark sites to bolster populations.For river users, the advice is simple but critical: Check, Clean, Dry.Check clothing and equipment for mud, aquatic animals or plant material and remove anything found.Clean everything thoroughly as soon as possible, using hot water where feasible.Dry for at least 48 hours, or use a suitable disinfectant before using gear elsewhere.Anyone who sees crayfish, alive or dead, is urged to leave them in place and report sightings to the Environment Agency, as it is illegal to handle or remove crayfish without the correct licences.A cautionary tale for invasive species policyThe story of signal crayfish in the UK is a clear example of how short-term economic decisions can create long-term ecological costs. What began as a promising aquaculture venture in the 1970s has become a persistent threat to native biodiversity, riverbank stability and the future of the white-clawed crayfish.Today, the focus is on containment, conservation and public awareness: protecting remaining strongholds, expanding ark sites and ensuring that people who enjoy rivers and lakes understand their role in preventing further spread. For policymakers, the signal crayfish episode underpins stricter rules on non-native species and reinforces the principle that preventing introductions is far easier, and cheaper, than trying to reverse them once they take hold.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Singapore will pay about $55,000 in support for each child; why the country is paying parents to have babies
articles.summary: World News: Singapore has a problem that money alone has not been able to solve. People there are having fewer children. Now the country is trying a bigger, longe.
articles.body: Singapore has a problem that money alone has not been able to solve. People there are having fewer children. Now the country is trying a bigger, longer-term approach. Singapore will provide almost S$70,000 (around US$55,000 or roughly Rs 47 lakh) in direct financial support for every Singaporean child, from birth until the child turns 17.The announcement was made by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong during Singapore's National Day Rally on August 23. But the headline figure needs some context. This is not a S$70,000 cheque that parents receive after having a baby. The amount is spread across different forms of support, including cash payments, healthcare-related grants, child credits and education support.The move comes as Singapore's fertility rate has fallen to its lowest recorded level. According to Singapore's Department of Statistics, the country's resident total fertility rate fell from 0.97 in 2024 to just 0.87 in 2025. There were 29,864 live births in 2025, down 11.4% from the previous year.The numbers explain why the government is trying something different.The money will follow the child, not just the birthSingapore already has one of Asia's better-known fertility-support systems, including its Baby Bonus Scheme. But the new SG Child Support Package changes the way that assistance is structured.According to Channel NewsAsia and various media, the new package will replace the existing Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Unlike the current system, the new package will provide the same baseline level of support for every Singaporean child, regardless of birth order.The support will also last longer. At present, much of the Baby Bonus support is concentrated in a child's early years. Under the new package, assistance will continue until the child turns 17.Starting April 1, 2027, each eligible newborn will receive a S$10,000 cash gift, paid in two installments within the first year.There will also be S$5,000 deposited into the child's Child Development Account, another S$5,000 in government co-matching of parents' CDA savings, S$2,000 in Child Credits every year for the first 16 years, a S$10,000 top-up to the Post-Secondary Education Account at age 17. Put together, these benefits bring the government's direct support to almost S$70,000 per child.Why Singapore is doing this nowSingapore's fertility rate has been falling for years despite repeated government efforts to encourage marriage and parenthood. The latest number 0.87 children per woman in 2025 is far below the roughly 2.1 level generally associated with population replacement in the absence of migration.This is not just about the number of babies being born. Fewer births today mean a smaller working-age population in the future, while longer life expectancy means more older people needing care and support. That creates pressure on everything from the workforce and healthcare to pensions, housing and the tax base.Singapore's government has therefore been looking at parenthood as a long-term national issue rather than simply a personal choice.The government knows money cannot solve everythingInterestingly, Prime Minister Wong did not suggest that a bigger payment would automatically make people have more children. In a recent speech, Wong acknowledged that the decision to have children is deeply personal and that government policies alone cannot make it happen. The aim, he said, is to make it easier for people who already want children to start and raise a family.The new package is not only about money. Singapore is also expanding support for parents who need time away from work to look after their children. The government has said it will take on a greater share of the cost of expanded childcare leave, reducing the burden on employers.There is another notable change. Under the existing Baby Bonus structure, some benefits are linked to the parents being lawfully married. The new SG Child Support Package will extend its benefits to all Singaporean children, regardless of their parents' marital status or family circumstances.So will S$70,000 actually make people have more babies?The government can make childcare cheaper. It can provide cash. It can support education. It can offer parents more leave and make housing easier to access. What it cannot do is make people want children. And that may be the hardest part of the problem Singapore is trying to solve.For now, the country is betting that if the financial and practical burden becomes lighter, at least some couples who are already thinking about having children may decide that the time is right.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal floods: Over 100 Indians missing; MEA issues helpline numbers
articles.summary: South Asia News: At least 384 travellers, including 105 Indians, have been reported missing following a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepalâs Rasuwa district.
articles.body: At least 384 travellers, including 105 Indians, have been reported missing following a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepalâs Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning, the Nepal Tourism Board said. The missing travellers include 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals.Of the 291 foreign nationals reported missing, others include citizens of Australia, the Netherlands, the United States, Malaysia, the United Kingdom and South Africa.The nationalities of several other foreign travellers are yet to be confirmed, while 37 have been listed as non-resident Indians (NRIs).The Embassy of India in Kathmandu has issued emergency helpline numbers for assistance and information regarding Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Nepal.Those seeking assistance can contact +977 985 131 6807 or +977 970 910 7500, the MEA said.The preliminary list was compiled using information from 10 tourism and travel agencies. The Tourism Board, Tourist Police and other tourism stakeholders are working with travel agencies, guides, local authorities and security agencies to verify the whereabouts and safety of those reported missing, as cited by Nepal News.The preliminary agency-wise records show that 92 travellers were associated with Trekkers Society, 71 with Samrat Tours & Travels, 55 with Leaf Holiday, 52 with Himalayan Glacier, 31 with Kailash Journey, 27 with Fishtail Tours & Travels, 20 with Alpine Eco Trek, 17 with Kathmandu Holiday Tours & Travels, 12 with Richa Tours & Travels and seven with Explore Vacation.Tourists in the affected areas have been advised to remain calm, stay updated through official channels and follow safety instructions issued by authorities.Those requiring emergency assistance can contact 1234, 1144 or the Tourist Police at 9851289445, Nepal News reported.They can also approach the nearest police or security personnel, local administration, travel agency, guide or tour operator.At least seventeen people have been confirmed dead and more than 25 rescued following the flash flood, Nepal Army officials said, according to local media reports.Police said four bodies were recovered from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot, near the Trishuli River. The Nepal Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police have been deployed for search-and-rescue operations, with 14 helicopters, drones and sniffer dogs being used to locate those still missing.The Nepal Army said six people were rescued from Syafrubesi, two from Mailung and four from Dhunche in Rasuwa. It has also established an emergency treatment centre at Military Training Centre No. 1 in Trishuli.Four Armed Police Force personnel were initially reported missing from Rasuwa, while another report said nine personnel stationed at Timure, near the Nepal-China border, remained unaccounted for.A sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River struck the Rasuwagadhi-Timure area at around 9 am local time, affecting Rasuwa as well as parts of the neighbouring Nuwakot and Dhading districts.The flooding washed away vehicles, goods, bridges and other infrastructure, while several hydropower projects also suffered damage.Amid concerns over a potential flood threat in Bihar following heavy rainfall in Nepal, Union home minister Amit Shah spoke to Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the phone, news agency ANI reported.Shah assured the Bihar government of all possible assistance to deal with the situation, while the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is being mobilised to respond to any emergency.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath also expressed concern over the flood situation in Nepal and directed authorities in vulnerable districts to remain alert.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Delhi court convicts Sukesh Chandrasekhar for posing as SC judge to seek bail
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted alleged conman Sukesh Chandrasekhar for impersonating a sitting Supreme Court judge to influence a special judg.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted alleged conman Sukesh Chandrasekhar for impersonating a sitting Supreme Court judge to influence a special judge into granting him bail in a 2017 corruption case.The court described the act as a "direct affront" to the independence and sanctity of the judicial process, news agency PTI reported.Chief judicial magistrate Harshita Mishra held Chandrasekhar guilty under IPC Sections 170 (personating a public servant), 189 (threat of injury to a public servant) and 507 (criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication).The court will hear arguments on the quantum of sentence on August 27.In an order dated August 20, the court said, "The present case shall for posterity remain a reminder that the majesty of law does not reside in the voice of an individual, however authoritative it may sound over a telephone, but in the integrity of the judicial process itself."The case relates to a phone call made on April 28, 2017, when Chandrasekhar was in police custody in connection with the corruption case.According to the prosecution, he gained access to the mobile phone of police constable Manjeet and used it to contact the official landline and mobile phone of Poonam Chaudhary, then special judge handling Prevention of Corruption Act cases.The court said Chandrasekhar initially impersonated the private secretary of a then sitting Supreme Court judge and later impersonated the judge himself.He allegedly sought to persuade Chaudhary to grant him bail at the earliest and threatened her with adverse professional consequences if she did not comply, PTI reported."A courtroom may be entered through its doors, but justice cannot be entered through the backdoor of impersonation, intimidation or manufactured authority. The accused attempted precisely such a backdoor entry into the judicial process. The evidence has closed that door," the court said.The judge said the case was qualitatively different from an ordinary cheating or impersonation matter as the alleged conduct sought to undermine judicial independence by invoking the authority of the country's highest court to influence another judicial officer."The court also finds it necessary to record that the conduct of the accused constitutes a direct affront to the independence and sanctity of the judicial process. Courts decide cases on the basis of law and evidence, not on the basis of telephone calls purporting to emanate from persons occupying positions of authority," the judge said.The court said the prosecution had established beyond reasonable doubt that Chandrasekhar deliberately assumed the identity of a Supreme Court judge to interfere with the administration of justice."The accused sought to use that borrowed authority not for any legitimate purpose, but to procure a judicial outcome favourable to himself. The brazenness of the attempt cannot dilute the offence; rather, it demonstrates the deliberateness with which the criminal design was executed," the judge said.It held that the impersonation was not incidental but "the very instrument" used to achieve his unlawful objective, as he understood that the words of a Supreme Court judge would carry an authority his own identity could not command.The court also found the ingredients of IPC Section 189 (threat of injury to public servant) made out, saying Chandrasekhar attempted to induce a judicial officer to exercise her discretion in a particular manner by invoking the supposed authority of a superior constitutional court.It further held that the anonymous nature of the communication attracted IPC Section 507 (criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication), PTI reported.Calling the conduct a direct affront to the judicial process, the court said allowing such attempts to be treated as mere deception could embolden people to circumvent courtrooms by manufacturing authority outside them."The judicial process cannot be allowed to become vulnerable to such manufactured commands," it said.The court, however, also directed Delhi Police to re-examine the role of constable Manjeet, including how Chandrasekhar obtained access to his mobile phone, whether it was locked, who knew its password and why the alleged use of the phone was not promptly reported.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
