articles.title: CIA chief held talks with Russian intelligence services, Kremlin says
articles.summary: John Ratcliffe travelled to the Russian capital on Tuesday in a rare and unannounced visit.
articles.body:
The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) met figures from Russia's intelligence services during his unannounced visit to Moscow on Tuesday, the Kremlin has confirmed.

John Ratcliffe travelled to the Russian capital on Tuesday but neither side has shed any light on what prompted the unconventional meeting or what was discussed.

It is rare for American senior intelligence leaders to travel to Russia, with the last comparable meeting taking place in the months leading up to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow on board a military plane which left later the same day.

The Kremlin ruled out speculation the CIA head met Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"There were contacts with the intelligence services," Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

"There were no meetings with the president of Russia. That's all I can say on the subject. Naturally, President Putin is briefed immediately about everything," he added.

Peskov made the comments in response to a question at his daily press briefing from a reporter at the Russian newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, who asked if Vladimir Putin was informed about the CIA chief meetings and "at what level" they were held.

Putin's spokesman was also asked by the BBC's Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg what was the topic of the CIA talks.

"I have nothing to add to what I've already said on the subject," Peskov replied.

It was too early to say what impact this meeting would have over repairing bilateral US-Russian relations, he said, telling reporters: "How much this will impact the overall process of recovering our bilateral relations from the profound crisis they're currently in, it is premature to say."

But contacts between intelligence agencies are "a positive phenomenon, a positive process," Peskov added, saying they often continue "even during the most difficult moments" in relations between the two countries.

Ahead of the trip, the US told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be travelling to Moscow and asked Kyiv to suspend strikes until they had left, a senior Ukrainian official told CBS.

There has been no official comment on Ratcliffe's visitfrom the CIA, White House or Pentagon.

Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit Russia during President Donald Trump's second term.

The last time a CIA director visited Moscow was in November 2021, when William Burns warned Russia against sending troops into Ukraine. Weeks later, the Kremlin launched its full-scale war on Ukraine.

Since then, the US has had strained relations with Russia, which has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions.

Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled.

John Foreman, who served as a British military attaché to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told Radio 4's PM programme: "The Americans don't normally send such a high ranking official to Moscow unannounced at short notice unless something is up."

articles.title: Heart, hope and a steely determination: Dolly Parton's musical legacy
articles.summary: BBC music correspondent Mark Savage looks back on the legacy of the "irreplaceable" late singer.
articles.body:
But her guitar was banned from the set - so she made the beat by strumming her acrylic nails together.

The sound, she realised, was just like the typewriter used by her character, a married secretary who is constantly belittled and sexually harassed by her boss.

Excited, she ran over and sang the song to her co-stars Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, who was also the film's producer.

"Lily and I looked at each other and we had goosebumps," Fonda said. "And we knew, this is not just a movie song, this is an anthem."

Taylor Swift and Beyoncé lead tributes after death of 'bold and brilliant' Dolly Parton

How Dolly Parton told her life story through six iconic songs

'If you want the rainbow, you gotta put up with the rain': The wit and wisdom of Dolly Parton

Released in November 1980, 9 To 5 became Parton's only US number one as a solo artist, and earned her an Oscar nomination for best song.

She loved to tell the fingernail story, but 9 To 5 has another legacy - for its powerful statements about working life and women's place in the corporate world.

You can probably sing the hook off the top of your head. " Working 9 To 5 / What a way to make a living! " It's jaunty and catchy. The sentiment is universal. Work sucks.

But dig deeper and Dolly's expressing real fury.

" It's a rich man's game, no matter what they call it / And you spend your life putting money in his wallet ," she sings. " They just use your mind and they never give you credit. "

The lyrics tapped into real frustrations and gave working women a voice.

But there's a reason why you might not have noticed the anger that fuels Dolly's song. She simply doesn't sing it that way - even though she had every right to, having navigated the sexism of the music industry from the age of 13.

Her early breakthrough came in 1967 when she was hired as the "girl singer" on The Porter Wagoner Show, a TV showcase for country singer Porter Wagoner that reached millions of viewers each week.

Together, they released 21 hit duets including Just Someone I Used to Know, If Teardrops Were Pennies and Please Don't Stop Loving Me.

But as Parton's star rose, she began to outshine her co-star. Eventually, she realised she needed to strike out as a solo artist – writing I Will Always Love You as a letter of apology to her former mentor. He responded by suing her for breach of contract in 1979, demanding $3m (£2,2m).

Wanting to avoid a lengthy court battle, Parton settled for about $1m.

"I made up my mind that if he could live with it, I could live without it," she wrote in her autobiography. "I suppose Porter has done all right with it. I am neither his conscience nor his accountant."

It was typical of the star's ability to radiate cheery goodwill that she never held a grudge against Wagoner, always crediting him with giving her a crucial career break, even after their relationship fell apart.

But she was nobody's fool. Take, for example, the battle over the rights to I Will Always Love You.

After it hit number one in the country charts, Elvis Presley called – he loved the song and wanted to record a cover.

"You cannot imagine how excited I am about this," she told him. "This is the greatest thing that's ever happened to me as a songwriter."

But the night before the recording session, his notoriously hard-nosed manager, Colonel Tom Parker, called Parton and told her Elvis wouldn't record the song unless she handed over half of the lucrative publishing rights.

"I said, 'Well, that throws a new light on this. Because I can't give you half the publishing. I'm gonna leave that to my family,'" Parton told Reba McEntire's podcast in 2020.

"And he said, 'Well, then we can't do it.' And I cried all night."

"I mean, it was like the worst thing," she told Country Music Television. "People were saying, 'You're nuts. It's Elvis Presley. Hell, I'd give him all of it.'

"I said, 'I can't.' I always wondered what it would sound like. I know he would have killed it [in a good way]."

When Whitney Houston recorded her blockbuster version of I Will Always Love You for The Bodyguard soundtrack in 1992, the country star still owned the rights and earned "enough money to buy Graceland", Presley's mansion.

Instead, she invested the money in a black neighbourhood in Nashville, Tennessee, saying she thought it was an apt way to honour Houston's legacy.

That determination to stand up for herself, and to value her music as more than just a commodity, is an essential part of Parton's legacy.

Without her example, would Taylor Swift have stood up to the hedge funds who bought her back catalogue, re-recording her biggest hits to rob them of royalties?

Perhaps not – but either way, Dolly approved.

"Smart!" she said when asked about Swift's masterplan. "She's so smart, she's so great, she's genius. I mean really, look at what she's doing! That's amazing!"

Mourning Parton's death, Swift acknowledged the star's "backbone of steel" in the struggle "to defend her own self worth as an artist".

Musically, her legacy is just as profound.

Parton was about six years old when she wrote her first song: Little Tiny Tasseltop, an ode to her favourite doll and its corn-silk hair.

For the rest of her career, she turned everyday details like those into songs of hope and heart.

Her 1971 classic Coat of Many Colors tells the profoundly moving story of Parton as a child being proud of the ragged, hand-sewn clothes her mother had made for her.

The 1974 concept album My Tennessee Mountain Home, meanwhile, is a musical autobiography that opens with Parton reciting the first letter she wrote home after moving to Nashville as a teenager.

" A couple of folks already told me that they might record a couple of my songs, so I'll be makin' enough money to get by ," she sang. " And I don't want you to be worrying about me bein' hungry or anything ."

The album cover is a photo of the two-room log cabin that was Parton's actual childhood home in the 1940s and 50s, and the rest of the songs paint an idyllic picture of her childhood.

Even when the family didn't have electricity and running water, she was determined to see the good in everyone and every situation.

" We might have been poor but we didn't know it / We'd heard that word but we didn't know what it meant. "

Her diaristic approach to songwriting also gave birth to hits like Jolene – written about a red-headed love rival – and All I Can Do, a heartfelt declaration of love to her husband, Carl Dean.

Funny and authentic, she captured the trials and tribulations of life in a way that was always relatable, even when her stage outfits and her hairstyle remained larger than life.

The feminist message of 9 To 5 was preceded by When Possession Gets Too Strong and Just Because I'm A Woman, which castigated double standards in relationships: " My mistakes are no worse than yours / Just because I'm a woman ."

And in an era where women were forced into gendered stereotypes – housewife, temptress, fallen woman, mixed-up girl – she satirised and sent up those roles, playing them to the hilt while emphasising her strength.

" I've always been misunderstood because of how I look ," she sang on 2008's Backwood Barbie. " Don't judge me by the cover, cos I'm a real good book ."

Words like those inspired generations of women to be who they were, not who the world perceived them as.

And she used her music to unite people, even as much of the country music establishment entrenched itself in conservatism.

In 2002, at the House of Blues in Los Angeles, Parton even replaced the name Jolene with "drag queen" as a crowd of drag performers looked on.

Outside music, her philanthropy gave scholarships to impoverished students and supplied more than 200 million books to young readers.

Significantly, none of the country stars she inspired were ever billed as "the next Dolly Parton" because no-one did it like Dolly. She was unique. Irreplaceable. Unreproducible.

A legend in her lifetime, and now beyond.

articles.title: Ex-chief constable being investigated by IOPC over Israeli fan ban
articles.summary: Craig Guildford, three police officers and a staff member face IOPC investigation.
articles.body:
The former chief constable of West Midlands Police is being investigated by the police watchdog for gross misconduct over the banning of Israeli Maccabi Tel Aviv fans from a match against Aston Villa.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has given notice that it is investigating Craig Guildford, as well as three police officers and a staff member.

An independent investigation was launched by the IOPC in January to examine the involvement of West Midlands Police officers in the planning and preparation of the match at Villa Park on 6 November 2025.

The ban attracted national and international debate, with the government saying it would do everything in its power to overturn it.

Maccabi supporters were barred from travelling to the game following safety concerns based on an inaccurate report prepared by West Midlands Police.

Eight errors were found in the report, including overstating Maccabi supporters' role in disorder in Amsterdam in 2024, and a reference to a non-existent game between Maccabi and West Ham, said to have been produced by Microsoft Copilot.

The decision to impose the ban was made by Birmingham's Safety Advisory Group (SAG), which included representatives from bodies including West Midlands Police and Birmingham City Council.

The IOPC said evidence indicated that Guildford "may have had oversight on an intelligence briefing document presented to the safety advisory group (SAG) that was later reported to have contained inaccuracies and misleading information".

It is alleged the briefing document "gave an imbalanced view of the risk away fans posed", contributing to the decision to ban the supporters.

The police watchdog added: "We consider Mr Guildford may have failed to ensure due diligence and the highest level of scrutiny over such an influential document."

Guildford retired from the force after both Downing Street and the home secretary said they had lost confidence in his leadership .

Announcing his retirement, Guildford did not offer an apology and blamed what he described as the "political and media frenzy" for his decision to step down.

A senior serving officer, who played a lead role in compiling the briefing, is under investigation for allegedly failing to ensure its accuracy.

The watchdog said the officer may not have accurately represented some information which could have resulted in the briefing "lacking impartiality".

They are also examining whether the officer "may have failed to appropriately handle sensitive intelligence" contained in the report, before it was shared with SAG members.

The staff member, who was involved in researching and compiling intelligence for the game, is alleged to have sourced inaccurate information from AI searches and took no subsequent action to help ensure it was not included in briefings.

Two other senior serving officers who played important roles in the force's planning for the game have been notified they are being investigated for potential misconduct.

It is alleged one was not sufficiently diligent in the exercise of their duties in overseeing the operation, including balancing operational needs alongside engaging with local Jewish communities, and that they displayed a lack of impartiality towards Maccabi fans in both external and internal communications.

The other officer will be investigated in relation to their oversight of the briefing document and an allegation that they too lacked balance in references to Maccabi supporters.

A dedicated investigation team at the IOPC has examined more than 600 pieces of evidence, including operational documents, reports, intelligence research, minutes of meetings, and a large volume of correspondence including emails and messages.

The IOPC's director of engagement, Derrick Campbell, said: "Our investigation to date has been to assess whether there is an indication anyone may have breached one or more of the standards of police professional behaviour.

"We have examined a wealth of material, hundreds of pieces of evidence, and believe there is an indication some people serving with the police may potentially have behaved in a manner that could justify disciplinary proceedings.

"They have been informed their conduct will be investigated. At the end of our investigation, we will decide if anyone has a case to answer and should face a misconduct meeting or hearing."

Campbell added that the serving of notices did not necessarily mean that disciplinary proceedings would follow, saying all decisions would be kept under review as the investigation progressed.

West Midlands Police's temporary deputy chief constable, Jen Mattinson, said that she undertook a voluntary referral to the IOPC on her first full day in the role regarding conduct matters by senior officers and staff.

"This referral was made prior to the IOPC announcement to use their 'power of initiative' to independently investigate if any officer or staff member may have a case to answer for misconduct," Mattinson said.

"We recognise that the public's trust in West Midlands Police has been damaged by this event and we have worked hard over the last seven months - and continue to do so - to rebuild confidence in the force.

"We will continue to fully engage and cooperate with the IOPC as their work continues."

West Midlands Police admitted that it "overstated the evidence" used to make the decision to ban the Maccabi Tel Aviv fans, in documents released in January .

The force said "we did not engage early enough with the local Jewish community", and indicated there was now a ban on AI use after its evidence included a match that did not take place.

Furthermore, it said its operations would have lasted four days, involved multiple forces, and cost more than £5m, if 2,500 away fans had attended.

articles.title: Dollar nudges higher ahead of US inflation data; Aussie gains on rate bets
articles.summary: By Alun John and Gregor Stuart Hunter LONDON/SINGAPORE, Aug 26 (Reuters) - The dollar edged higher but remained range-bound against major peers on Wednesday...
articles.body:
LONDON/SINGAPORE, Aug 26 (Reuters) - The dollar edged higher but remained range-bound against major peers on Wednesday as investors awaited U.S. inflation data that could set the tone ahead of the Jackson Hole symposium ‌of central bankers later this week.

The most notable mover was the Australian dollar, which hit $0.71865, its highest level in three ‌months, after data showed the trimmed mean CPI gauge, the Reserve Bank of Australia's preferred measure of cost-of-living pressures, rose at a faster-than-expected annual rate of 3.6%.

It was ​last up 0.24%, just below that level.

"With underlying inflation showing no signs of slowing, there's still a risk that the RBA will deliver another rate hike over the coming months," Capital Economics analysts wrote in a research note.

Aside from the Swiss franc, against which the dollar rose 0.3% to 0.8036 francs, moves in the most traded currency pairs were muted ahead of a potentially pivotal few days for markets.

The dollar climbed 0.1% against ‌the Japanese yen to 158.95 yen, while sterling ⁠slipped 0.2% to $1.3624.

The euro was also a touch weaker at $1.1664, shrugging off a Reuters report citing sources saying ECB policymakers are prepared to raise interest rates at their September meeting but have little appetite to signal ⁠further tightening.

Traders were focused on the release of July U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data later in the day, ahead of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's keynote speech at Jackson Hole on Friday.

The conference, with its global audience and intense media coverage, offers Fed officials a high-profile platform ​to signal ​policy thinking or reinforce existing messages.

PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. ​Economists polled by Reuters expect core PCE, which excludes ‌food and energy, to have risen 3.3% in July from a year earlier, unchanged from June and well above the Fed's 2% target.

If forecasts prove correct, traders will look for clues from Warsh on whether further rate hikes may be needed to bring inflation back to target. Some analysts say the recent rise in long-dated Treasury yields suggests the Fed may need to do more.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision to intervene in the market in an attempt to lower bond yields has added another layer of complexity, though analysts do not expect a ‌great deal of explanation from Warsh's remarks.

"Normally, this would be an event awaited ​with great anticipation where the Fed would be prepared to lay out its future ​monetary policy strategy or even signal major policy regime shifts," ​said Benoit Anne, senior managing director at MFS Investment Management.

articles.body: Three US Secret Service officials have been placed on administrative leave pending an investigation into potential misconduct, with the agency's Office of Professional Responsibility conducting the probe.The officials were working in non-law enforcement roles, the Secret Service said, according to the Associated Press. The agency did not disclose what prompted the action or provide details about the alleged misconduct.The three employees include Chief of Communications Anthony Guglielmi and two other members of the Secret Service's communications office. Their security clearances and access to work devices have also been suspended as part of the investigation, according to US officials cited by CBS.The development comes as the Secret Service faces increased scrutiny over security arrangements for President Donald Trump, who has been the target of at least three assassination plots over the past two years.In April, an armed man breached security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, which Trump was attending, AP reported.The agency has also recently investigated a member of Vice President JD Vance's security detail over allegations of leaking sensitive information.The probe followed a July report by MS NOW about frustration among some agents over last-minute travel requests involving Vance and his family.The Secret Service has also drawn attention over Trump's recent departure from Turkey.Trump acknowledged earlier this month that he had been moved to a different aircraft because the Secret Service and military were concerned about a possible Iranian assassination threat.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Islamabad PIMS hospital fire: Witnesses say rescue was delayed as blaze killed 14 babies
articles.summary: A hospital official told the BBC that the door to the ward was not locked, but manned with security guards, to protect the babies.
articles.body:
It was just after dawn on Wednesday morning at a maternity ward in the Pakistani capital when a horrific blaze erupted.

It would go on to kill 14 infants as parents say they waited hours for help to arrive.

Hivsa Walid was near the room at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital with her sister-in-law, who had given birth days earlier. She initially heard a shout and thought a patient had died - but then she saw smoke.

The pair fled with the baby, who is so small she does not yet have a name.

"We didn't even think about our belongings. We just grabbed the baby and rushed downstairs.

"Some patients had delivered their babies just that night. I don't even know how we managed to get down - it was all a blur."

The fire broke out in an air-conditioning unit on the third floor of the mother and child unit at PIMS, one of the main state-run hospitals in Islamabad. Only one of the 15 babies present was saved.

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP news agency there was a long wait for rescue workers. "I lost my daughter. She was only three days old," he said.

Jaweria, the mother of another victim, told AFP news agency the door to the maternity ward was locked.

"For two hours I kept crying and wailing," she said. "Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate."

"Why did the doctors leave the children there?" she asks.

"To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them."

Rana Imran Sikander, the hospital's executive director, told the BBC the ward's door was not locked but was manned. He cited the need to protect babies from being stolen, something that has happened before at government hospitals.

Walid suggested PIMS's safety protocols were inadequate, despite it being a major hospital. "There should have been fire extinguishers and protocols, but no one was doing anything - everyone was just running."

The father of a baby who died told Reuters he had been visiting the ward for eight days and the building had "no fire security, no proper exits".

"All doors were closed, only one door was for us to visit our children. They kept the other doors locked because they feared we would come to see our children too often."

Several eyewitnesses have claimed duty staff were not around.

People had to "break the door down" and rescue teams were forced to smash the windows to control the flames, a witness who did not give her name told AFP.

Abdul Ghafoor, another witness, told AFP he tried to get into the building to rescue patients but couldn't reach the maternity ward.

"There was thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped," he said. "Rescue teams arrived after almost two hours."

Islamabad's Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf has said rescue teams reached the scene "immediately" after the emergency call was first made, according to AFP.

PIMS is one of the biggest hospitals in Pakistan's capital, with 156 beds in its maternal and child health unit.

Pakistan has dealt with a number of major fires in recent years, with poor safety laws, building codes and lax enforcement often blamed for steep death tolls.

Survivors of a fire which killed dozens at a Karachi shopping mall in January this year said locked exits likely contributed to the high number of fatalities.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has expressed his "deep sorrow and heartfelt regret" over the latest blaze, and instructed authorities to "conduct an immediate investigation", according to a statement from his office.

He has also suspended Federal Health Secretary Aslam Ghauri, a top official in the health department.

"Such a situation with children is irreparable", the statement said.

articles.title: Sark could protect 30% of waters in marine plan
articles.summary: The proposal would give added protection to about 50 sq miles (128.8 sq km) of sea around Sark.
articles.body:
An island wants to protect 30% of its waters under plans aimed at safeguarding marine life.

The proposal would see about 50 sq miles (128.8 sq km) of sea around Sark in the Channel Islands receive additional protection under plans developed by the island's agriculture, environment and sea fisheries committee with support from the Blue Marine Foundation, local fishermen and marine experts.

Freddie Watson, Channel Islands project manager at Blue Marine Foundation, told BBC Radio Guernsey that marine protection could help safeguard sensitive habitats while supporting sustainable fishing.

The proposal is expected to be submitted to the island's governing Chief Pleas by 1 September.

Watson explained that evidence had been used to identify important habitats, including previously unmapped areas of seagrass, so protection could be focused where it was needed most.

The waters around Sark are home to species including European spiny lobster, rays, catsharks, octopus and pink sea fans.

Watson said the plans formed part of a wider effort across the Channel Islands to safeguard marine environments, including a plan to protect more than 20% of Jersey's waters.

Watson said stronger protection could bring benefits for both wildlife and people by helping to sustain fish stocks and preserve habitats that support marine biodiversity.

He added: "Some of those habitats are really important at drawing down and locking away carbon."

The Sark proposal depends on political approval, with members of Chief Pleas expected to debate the plans on 30 September.

There are different ways to invest in gold, and each has pros and cons. Four common options are:

Physical gold includes jewelry, gold bars, and gold coins. Some prefer physical gold over other forms because it's tangible and easy to purchase. You can easily buy a gold necklace at the mall or gold bars at Costco ( COST ).

The advantages of physical gold include:

Readily accessible for use: If you keep your physical gold at home, it is easily available to use as a medium of exchange in an economic emergency.

No added volatility or ongoing fees: If you hold the gold yourself, "you eliminate counterparty risk and storage fees or expense ratios," explained Brett Elliott, director of content and SEO at American Precious Metals Exchange (APMEX). You also avoid the added business volatility associated with gold mining stocks, as explained below.

The disadvantages of physical gold include:

Risk of theft or loss: Physical gold must be properly secured. You can store it at home for free, or invest in third-party storage and insurance. Remember that fees associated with storage or insurance dilute your returns.

Lower liquidity: Physical gold is less liquid — that is, harder to sell quickly — than stocks or ETFs. Also, if you are not using the gold as a medium of exchange, you must find a dealer and pay a markup on the sale.

Gold mining stocks are equity positions in gold miners. They can be volatile because their profits are tied to gold prices, plus these companies are heavily exposed to "geopolitical risks and management risks" according to Vince Stanzione, CEO and founder at financial publisher First Information. To manage the volatility, many investors prefer diversified gold mining funds over individual mining stocks.

The advantages of gold mining stocks include:

Greater liquidity: Large-cap gold mining stocks like Barrick Gold Corporation ( B ) and Franco-Nevada Corporation ( FNV ) generally enjoy a narrow bid-ask spread, which is a sign of liquidity. The bid-ask spread is the difference between what buyers will pay and what sellers will accept.

No storage requirements: Stocks live in your brokerage account and do not consume physical space. In normal times, this is an advantage. In an economic catastrophe, this could be a disadvantage if brokers or the stock market are temporarily shut down.

The disadvantages of owning gold mining stocks include:

Greater volatility: "Gold investing through gold mining companies adds another layer of risk," explained Thomas Winmill, portfolio manager at mutual fund company Midas Funds. From 2000 to 2020, gold mining stocks have risen and fallen faster than gold spot prices. In recent years, gold mining stocks have trended down as gold spot prices have gained value.

No utility as a medium of exchange: Gold mining stocks can appreciate, but they have no direct utility as a medium of exchange.

Gold ETFs are funds that track the price of gold. They can invest in physical gold stores, gold mining stocks, gold futures, or some combination of these. The largest gold ETF in terms of total assets is SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ), which is backed by physical gold stored in vaults.

Easy to store: Like gold mining stocks, ETF shares are digital assets with no storage requirements.

Greater liquidity: Shares of the most popular gold ETFs, like SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) and iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ), are heavily traded. Steady demand makes them easy to sell.

Tied directly to gold prices: ETFs backed by physical gold track the spot price of gold, which is usually less volatile than gold mining stocks or gold mining ETFs.

Fund fees: Funds charge fees, which dilute returns over time. For context, the expense ratio of SPDR Gold Shares is 0.40%. This translates to $4 in fees annually for every $1,000 invested.

No utility as a medium of exchange: As with gold mining stocks, you probably cannot use ETF shares to trade for food in an economic emergency.

Gold futures are standardized contracts to purchase gold on a future date at a specific price. The contracts often represent 100 troy ounces. According to Stanzione, among gold investing options, gold futures carry "the highest risk and are best left to professional traders."

Leverage: You can control a large amount of gold with a low capital outlay.

Convenience: You don't need to store physical gold to earn from its price changes.

The disadvantages of investing in gold futures are:

Risk: Leverage amplifies gains and losses. This is always risky, but especially so with an unpredictable asset like gold.

Complexity: The complexity of futures contracts can be off-putting to many retail investors.

articles.title: How Dolly Parton helped the world - from children's books to supporting Covid vaccine
articles.summary: The late singer-songwriter's charity causes were as eclectic as her music, but she had a personal connection to each one.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton will not only be remembered for her iconic songs and Southern charm, but also for her philanthropic work.

Throughout her life, she supported communities in need, especially in her home state of Tennessee. She funded medical research that led to one of the first Covid-19 vaccines, donated to wildfire victims and even helped the once-endangered bald eagle, America's national bird.

But it is her Imagination Library - the mainstay of her charity work - that has helped millions of children learn to read by sending out free books.

The programme was inspired by her father who couldn't read or write.

"I think deep down inside, my daddy was prouder of [the library] than he even was of my career," she wrote.

Parton established her non-profit organisation, the Dollywood Foundation, in 1988, to help bolster children's education. Its efforts are practical - like sending out books - and often goes directly to the grass roots, where it can really make a difference, fast.

In the early 90s, Parton said she'd give every seventh and eighth-grade student (ages 12 to 14) in Sevier County, Tennessee, where she grew up, $500 if they graduated high school. They had to have a buddy, to keep each other in check - which in turn made more children graduate.

Sure, it was a bit of a bribe, but it worked - the drop out rate went from 35% to 6%, according to the foundation's website.

"I'm kind of addicted to the feeling of giving," she once said. "Knowing that I'm doing something good for someone else."

Parton was awarded the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in 2022, which honoured her as "one of the entertainment world's most generous philanthropists".

'All children should grow up in a home full of books'

Dolly Parton was one of 12 children born into a poor family that lived in a one-bedroom cabin in the Smoky Mountains. Her hardworking father, Robert Lee Parton, was a tobacco farmer.

"He was the smartest man I have ever known but I know in my heart his inability to read probably kept him from fulfilling all of his dreams," Dolly wrote.

Inspired by this, the Imagination Library was launched in 1995, with the help of Robert Parton. It sends out free books to children younger than five every month.

The programme was originally set up just for those in Sevier County - but it quickly went national and then global. The Imagination Library now sends books to children across the US, Canada, UK, Ireland and Australia.

According to its website, more than 332.4 million books have been sent out.

For many children who have never owned their own book, it is a special gift just for them.

"It's the fact they get recognised," Parton once said. "They get this little book with their little name on it in the mail, and they feel special... they know that somebody out there is thinking of them."

"That vision she had about books and this understanding of sharing stories was remarkable," Eileen Driver, the chair of the Stokesley Imagination Library in the UK, told the BBC's Radio Tees.

Scottish National Party councillor, Lee Mills - admittedly a superfan from a young age - said when he was elected he set out to bring the Imagination Library to Dundee.

"Dolly's legacy will last with every page turned of a children's book. I will do my utmost best to ensure that this is delivered to every child in Scotland," he told the BBC.

British author Selina Brown, whose book My Rice is Best was one of those selected to be distributed, told the BBC it was quite emotional to see 14,000 copies of her book being packed up, ready to post.

"For my book in particular, the protagonist is black. It helps with representation, it helps with real life situations and having a book that speaks directly to you and speaks to a different world is important."

During Covid, Parton started reading some of the books aloud, in recordings on YouTube for children - many of whom didn't know who she was.

"You mean she sings, too?" exclaimed one boy when he found out, Linda Jinnette Cooper wrote on the library's Facebook page.

In 2020, as the Covid-19 pandemic gripped the world, Parton encouraged people to get vaccinated and donated $1m (Â£716,000) to the Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, which helped fund the Moderna vaccine.

A portion of the money went towards funding an early stage-trial of the Moderna vaccine, which found it to offer nearly 95% protection against severe Covid-19.

Reimagining her hit song, Jolene, Parton changed the lyrics to "vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, I'm begging of you, please don't hesitate".

She showed herself being injected, saying: "I'm old enough to get it and I'm smart enough to get it."

Parton donated to medical research several times over the years.

A benefit concert in 2007 raised $1m for a new hospital and cancer centre in Sevier County, which includes a Dolly Parton Center for Women's Services.

Ten years later, she released a children's album, I Believe in You, and donated another $1m, this time to Nashville's Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, after her niece was treated for leukaemia there.

She donated yet another $1m to the hospital a few years later, this time to help paediatric infectious disease research.

"I love children," Parton said in a statement at the time. "No child should ever have to suffer, and I'm willing to do my part to try and keep as many of them as I can as healthy and safe as possible."

And earlier this year, the East Tennessee Children's Hospital announced it would be renamed to the Dolly Parton Children's Hospital, after the star partnered with the not-for-profit facility.

The Dollywood Foundation has a scholarships programme for high school seniors, which offers $15,000 to five students "who have a dream they wish to pursue".

It has also donated to the Salvation Army and helped the victims of several disasters in Tennessee.

After a deadly fire in Sevier County in 2016, Parton held a telethon that raised more than $13m. Kenny Rogers, Chris Stapleton, Reba McEntire and Cyndi Lauper were some of the big names who joined the event.

Parton continued her support by pledging $1,000 per month for six months to about 900 families who had lost their homes.

Five years later, when Middle Tennessee was devastated by flooding, Parton helped to raise $700,000 for residents.

"I'm just so proud to have been a part of anything that's good and that's making life a little better for people," she told Good Morning America the same year.

Her Dollywood amusement park has a lot more than rollercoasters - it's also home to the largest sanctuary for non-releasable bald eagles in the world.

Managed by the American Eagle Foundation, its rehabilitation and breeding work has won awards and in 2007, the bald eagle was removed from the endangered species list.

In 2022, Parton's charity work to improve education was extended to adults, when it was announced that any Dollywood employee - whether they were seasonal, part-time or full-time, would have 100% of their tuition and books paid for if they furthered their education.

In announcing her death on Tuesday, Parton's team asked fans to donate to the Imagination Library, instead of sending flowers, so that her legacy can continue for many years to come.

"When I'm done, I can rest in peace knowing I've done my best," Parton once said.

"I hope that when my time comes, I'll leave something behind that others can use to lift themselves up."

articles.title: Chinese-Eswatini relations: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally over security risks
articles.summary: Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
articles.body:
China's foreign ministry has told its citizens to leave the southern African kingdom of Eswatini over "security risks".

The ministry cited "rampant cyber fraud and criminal activities associated with gambling" as among its security concerns, but did not give details.

It suggested its citizens relocate as soon as possible to "relatively safer" countries such as neighbouring South Africa.

Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which China claims as part of its territory.

On Tuesday, the privately owned Times of Eswatini news site reported that 40 Chinese nationals have been in detention since last month after being arrested while trying to leave the country.

They were first arrested - along with dozens of other foreign nationals - in March during raids on alleged illegal online gambling centres in the main city, Mbabane, and surrounding areas, the news site reported.

The group's lawyers had written to the attorney general and home affairs ministry, stating that they had pleaded guilty to immigration-related offences and had paid fines imposed by the courts, the news site reported.

The 40 were then released on the orders of the High Court, and their re-arrest was unlawful, the lawyers were quoted as saying.

The Eswatini government has not yet commented.

In its advisory to its citizens, China says those who insist on travelling to or staying in the country will face "extremely high security risks, and the timeliness of assistance may be affected".

It is unclear how many Chinese citizens work or live in Eswatini.

China has for years pressured countries to end diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

In April, Taiwan accused Beijing of trying to derail its President Lai Ching-te's travel to Eswatini by pressuring nearby countries to revoke overflight permits.

The trip, originally planned for 22-26 April to mark the 40th anniversary of Eswatini's King Mswati III's accession, was cancelled following the development.

Lai eventually travelled to Eswatini in May, without saying how he reached the country. None of the governments had announced the trip beforehand.

Following the visit, Beijing's foreign ministry said that Lai had become "an international laughing stock".

Earlier this year, China scrapped tariffs for all African countries, except Eswatini.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaks: Rockstar issues statement over online clips
articles.summary: The game developer says the unauthorised footage has caused "heartbreak" for those working on the title.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

Copies of clips were quickly taken down from social media sites via copyright strikes, where the owner of a work can request its removal.

And, on Friday, Rockstar's parent company Take Two Interactive launched legal proceedings regarding the leaks in a New York court.

Rockstar acknowledged players had been waiting for it to address the leaked footage, and said it was "unfortunate the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers".

It also thanked fans who sent messages of support over the past week, adding: "Your words have meant more to the team than you can imagine."

The group behind the leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch .

Not everyone is convinced, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

GTA 6, due to be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox consoles in November, is still expected to be the biggest video game launch of the decade.

The previous game in the series, GTA 5, also broke records when it came out in 2013 and has sold more than 200 million copies since.

Two official trailers for the sixth game have almost 500 million combined views on YouTube, and the Netflix "extended look" on Thursday is being marketed as an event by the streaming service.

Next month the company is due to appear at an employment tribunal in Scotland to defend itself against claims it illegally sacked a group of ex-employees for trying to form a union .

It strongly denies the accusations, and says the workers were fired on the grounds of gross misconduct.

articles.title: Americans reported among hundreds missing in Nepal floods, tourism board says
articles.summary: At least three American tourists were reported among a "preliminary" toll.
articles.body:
At least three American tourists were reported among a "preliminary" toll of 384 missing people following serious flash flooding in Nepal, according to a statement posted to X by the Nepal Tourism Board.

The flooding occurred in the northern Rasuwa district, along the border with Tibet, at around 8:30 a.m. local time on Wednesday, authorities said.

The preliminary toll of the missing included 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, the Tourism Board said in its statement.

The three Americans were listed as traveling with a Nepali company called Fishtail Tours and Travel. The agency confirmed to ABC News that three American nationals are among the missing tourists traveling with them.

Efforts to locate and rescue the missing tourists is ongoing, the company said, without providing any further information on their possible whereabouts or wellbeing.

The Nepal Tourism Board said that local tourism and law enforcement authorities were "working to verify the whereabouts and safety status of tourists and travelers who were in or traveling through the affected areas."

The U.S. Embassy in Kathmandu said in posts to X that it was "deeply saddened by the tragic loss of life and devastation" caused by the flooding. "We are closely tracking developments and remain in close contact with Nepali authorities," the embassy said.

The mission also urged Americans to avoid the affected areas and said it was working "to account for U.S. citizens who may have been affected."

Also among the foreign nationals listed as missing in the Tourism Board's preliminary count were Indian, Malaysian, British, South African, Dutch and Australian tourists.

Rescue operations for flood-affected people were ongoing via air transport as of Wednesday, the Nepali Army said in a post to X on Wednesday. The army urged people to adopt high vigilance and stay in safe places.

The flood reportedly inflicted casualties on the Chinese side of the border, at the Gyirong border crossing, according to the Chinese state-run Xinhua News Agency.

President Xi Jinping, the agency reported, ordered search and rescue efforts for those reported missing.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

articles.summary: US News: Michigan has awarded nearly $1.4 billion for land protection and recreation projects across the state. The Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund that .
articles.body: Michigan has awarded nearly $1.4 billion for land protection and recreation projects across the state. The Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund that was created in 1976, is also marking 50 years of a conservation fund that has used earnings from the stateâs oil, gas and mineral revenues to support public land and outdoor recreation.According to Michigan state government official site, the latest funding comes through Michiganâs fiscal year 2027 budget. It includes $45 million in Trust Fund grants for 75 land acquisition and park development projects. The grants are expected to combine with nearly $64 million in local and matching funds, creating a total investment of $108.9 million in public land and outdoor recreation.One of the biggest allocations is for the Keweenaw Peninsula. The Michigan Department of Natural Resources will receive $6.5 million to acquire nearly 22,650 acres. The land acquisition will consolidate state-managed land for recreation and natural resource protection.The funding also includes $1.5 million for the DNR to acquire 460 acres next to Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. The land includes wooded hills, trout streams and wildlife habitats. Another $5 million will help the DNR acquire more than 1,400 acres of forestland, including all of Turtle Lake and nearly two miles of the Turtle Creek corridor, to protect habitat and water quality in the Au Sable River watershed.Turning resource revenues into conservationThe Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund is a restricted fund established to support the public acquisition of land for resource protection and outdoor recreation. s The fund is financed through interest and earnings from revenues generated by state-owned oil, gas and mineral leases.The Trust Fund is administered by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources and was placed in Michiganâs Constitution for permanent protection. Over five decades, it has supported land purchases, land rights and improvements to outdoor recreation facilities across the state.According to DNR Director Scott Bowen,âSince its inception, the Trust Fund has awarded crucial grant dollars to local governments and state agencies for creative projects and acquisitions that greatly benefit residents and local economies in every county of the state.â75 projects receive fundingThe fiscal year 2027 budget supports projects across Michigan, covering both land acquisitions and improvements to existing parks and trails.Among the acquisition projects, East Bay Township will receive $4.8 million to acquire an easement on 333 acres known as the Ridge Nature Preserve. The project will protect public access and future trail connections to the Traverse Area Recreation and Transportation trail system.Saugatuck Township will receive $2.5 million to acquire 119 acres along the Kalamazoo River. The property includes more than 2,200 feet of river frontage and is planned as a destination park and nature preserve.The DNR will also receive $1.6 million to acquire 354 acres of oak-pine barrens habitat in Newaygo County. The acquisition will connect the east and west units of the Muskegon State Game Area.Other acquisitions include former railway land for the North Country National Scenic Trail and Michiganâs Iron Belle Trail, waterfront land along Pettyâs Bayou and additional land along the Grand River and Black River.The development grants will fund a wide range of improvements. Projects include accessible trails, playgrounds, boat launches, boardwalks, restrooms, parking areas, trailheads and waterfront facilities.The city of Grayling, for example, will receive $400,000 to build a 1.8-mile shared-use pathway along M-72. In Detroit, $400,000 will support an inclusive playground at Clemente Park, along with parking, a multi-sport court and landscaping.Other projects include a new accessible path through Bliss Park in Saginaw, improvements to Rosy Mound Natural Area in Ottawa County and a three-mile extension of the Blue Star Trail in Saugatuck Township.Fund has also shaped Detroit RiverfrontThe Trust Fundâs impact can also be seen along Detroitâs riverfront. In June, the Michigan DNR highlighted projects supported through decades of state and local partnerships.The Detroit Riverfront attracts about 3 million people each year and has received more than $45 million in Trust Fund-supported community investment through different projects.At Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Centennial Park, $5.7 million in Trust Fund support helped create connections to the riverfront, including the West Riverfront Connector. The 22-acre park has play areas, a water garden, a sport house and landscaped paths.The William G. Milliken State Park and Harbor has received $26.25 million in Trust Fund funding. Projects there include a 1,500-foot pedestrian trail, the final connection of the Detroit East Riverwalk through the park and land and easement acquisitions along the Detroit River.Trust Fund support also helped acquire 48,000 square feet of space in the historic Globe Building for the DNR Outdoor Adventure Center. articles.title: At least 19 dead and more than 380 tourists missing after flash flooding in Nepal
articles.summary: Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.
articles.body:
Over 380 tourists, mostly foreigners, were out of contact in Nepal on Wednesday after a massive flood tore through the border region with Tibet.

"A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board, noting authorities were working to verify the travellers' whereabouts.

"Nineteen bodies have been recovered so far. We are intensely coordinating the rescue and relief efforts. Many in our police force are also out of contact," Nepali police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said.

Videos shared by Nepal police and others on social media showed torrents of muddy water crashing through mountain valleys in the Himalayan district bordering China.

"I witnessed the flood sweep away eight or nine trucks, along with houses and people," Suman Chalise, a 34-year-old teacher, told AFP in Nuwakot district.

"It was absolutely heart-wrenching. I had not witnessed such devastation before."

The police spokesperson said earlier that authorities did not know the extent of the damage but said they had "alerted people who are staying near the riverside to relocate."

The Nepal Army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster response personnel to the affected area.

The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, has been damaged.

"The disaster has damaged the production, transmission and distribution facilities of the Authority...resulting in disruption of electricity supply," it said.

Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed "no anomalies" from China's side of the border.

"We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event," he said.

Several highways were also closed, Nepali authorities said.

Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that "a mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port" in Tibet.

Footage shared by the broadcaster, showed rushing water carrying tree branches and debris, as well as a flooded road.

State news agency Xinhua said Chinese President Xi Jinping had urged "all-out" rescue operations, but did not provide figures on injuries or deaths.

Xi said that "the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people...quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible," according to CCTV.

Traffic authorities in Tibet's Shigatse said roads in the area were "at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage" in a post on social media on Wednesday.

In July last year, 17 people went missing after a mudslide near the Gyirong Port, Xinhua reported at the time.

Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.

articles.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy shares his progress working with Rashee Rice
articles.summary: During Tuesday's press conference, Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy shared his progress working with Rashee Rice | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy spoke with reporters before practice on Tuesday. He shared his progress with wide receiver Rashee Rice as the team prepares for the 2026 season.

"Well, first of all, Rashee (Rice) is a very good player. His overall resume has spoken for itself. The thing I'm trying to get to know, and we're still working through this, is getting to know the person," said Bieniemy. "To see the things that make him click. What are the things that inspire him? What are some of the things that he loves to do off the field? It's all about building relationships with people. And so the thing that I love about Rashee, first and foremost, he's tough. He's very, very tough. Another thing, and I'm not saying this in a bad way, he's hardheaded."

The Chiefs are looking forward to having Rice for a full season after he missed multiple games last year due to suspension and injuries. Bieniemy is focused on getting the best version of Rice this season under his coaching.

"He's stubborn because he feels that he's good enough at certain things, and I like that because you got to get him to see it from a different point of view. And when he can see it from a different point of view with a set of different eyes, now it opens up his brain," said Bieniemy. "And I mean, you can see it resonate, and so those are the things that I've learned about him. Now, it's just about making sure we can get the continuous reps to get him back on track, to get him in game shape because we have to get it right. And on top of that, we got to make sure that all the little fine details that need to be executed are basically done within the next couple of weeks or so."

Rice finished last season with 53 catches for 571 yards and five touchdowns, averaging 10.8 yards per reception.

articles.title: Beau Stephens becomes important to Seahawks after Mason Richman injury
articles.summary: Rookie blocker Beau Stephens becomes important to the Seattle Seahawks after the Mason Richman injury.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks lost one rookie and one sophomore to season-ending injuries in the Week 2 preseason loss to the Tennessee Titans . Most notably, second-round safety Bud Clark suffered a broken ankle injury . Also, sophomore guard Mason Richman was placed on season-ending IR with an injury of his own.

Both injuries deliver a significant blow to the Seahawks' roster depth. Losing Richman makes rookie guard Beau Stephens even more important . The Seahawks are thinner at guard without Richman, and it could eventually force Stephens into a bigger role.

The Seahawks will start Grey Zabel and Anthony Bradford at guard for a second consecutive season. Richman was initially in the mix for a depth role behind them. With him landing on season-ending IR, Stephens and Christian Haynes are the unquestioned reserve guards.

Some even wondered if Haynes would be traded or released this offseason. That's also unlikely to happen following Richman's injury. Meanwhile, Stephens has been listed as Zabel's backup at left guard on the unofficial depth chart.

Having Richman gave the Seahawks another option at reserve guard. His absence could force Stephens and Haynes into bigger roles on the depth chart. A rookie fifth-round pick, Stephens has to be ready for whatever.

articles.title: Klay Thompson eyes 'redemption season' after move to Miami
articles.summary: Klay Thompson is eager to return to the postseason after the Dallas Mavericks finished with a 26-56 record a season ago.
articles.body:
Following his move to the Miami Heat , former Golden State Warriors guard Klay Thompson gave his thoughts on the newest chapter of his career. After signing with the Mavericks ahead of the 2024-25 season, things never went to plan for Thompson in Dallas , as the infamous Luka Doncic trade changed the team's outlook entirely. After averaging a career-low 11.7 points per game for the Mavericks in what ended up as a 26-56 season last year, the four-time champion felt it was time to move on.

Now in South Beach, Thompson has his sights set on a bounce-back season. In his introductory press conference with the Heat, Thompson said , "It's kind of a redemption season for me to show I can still make an impact on winning and do it consistently."

The former Washington State guard also revealed how much he missed playing in the playoffs, saying , "I just missed out on the postseason. I hate watching from home."

"That's all I want to do these next couple of years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run."

With a new look Heat roster that includes Giannis Antetokounmpo , Miami seems destined to improve on a 10th-place finish in the Eastern Conference last season.

articles.title: Ex-Arsenal Ramsdale requests Southampton u21 appearance
articles.summary: Former Gunner Aaron Ramsdale requested the chance to play for the Southampton u21s earlier this month, according to the club’s manager.Photo by George Wood/G...
articles.body:
Former Gunner Aaron Ramsdale requested the chance to play for the Southampton u21s earlier this month, according to the club's manager.

On August 14th, Aaron Ramsdale started for the Southampton u21s in a Premier League Cup match against Blackburn Rovers.

The match went very well, with the former Arsenal goalkeeper keeping a clean sheet in a 4-0 victory for the u21 side. But it obviously raised the question of why the 28-year-old was involved at all.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckhert provided the answer to the Daily Echo this week.

"He (Ramsdale) asked for minutes," Eckert said . "I have to say that he's been very professional from the very first day.

"We've had a conversation early on, and since I came in I've worked with Daniel [ Peretz ] and with Longy ( George Long ). We've been very clear about the situation. Daniel has signed as a number one and Longy as a number two for us going into the season. I've had that conversation with Rambo.

"I also told him he would get everything from us in the pre-season to get him in the best condition possible. It speaks for him that he wants to play.

"He just wants the feeling because there are some things that you just can't replicate in a training session."

Whilst the positive outing for the u21s will have been good for Ramsdale's fitness and confidence, he's still in a scenario where he has no realistic route to minutes with Southampton this season.

The goalkeeper had a relatively busy campaign in 2025/26, playing on loan with Newcastle United . He made 23 appearances in all competitions, but the club ultimately decided not to take up their purchase option.

If Ramsdale wants to play senior football this season, he likely needs to secure a transfer before next Tuesday's deadline. Arsenal will be watching on, knowing they hold a sell-on clause for the goalkeeper.

articles.title: Do the Titans have to keep RB Julius Chestnut?
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans reserve running back Julius Chestnut is once again battling for a 53-man roster spot.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will have a joint practice with the Chicago Bears on Thursday. They'll then play the preseason finale versus those same Bears on Saturday. Approximately 24 hours later, general manager Mike Borgonzi will be tasked with finalizing his initial 53-man roster.

Among Borgonzi's bigger decisions is at running back. The Titans are expected to roster four ball carriers. Tony Pollard , Tyjae Spears , and rookie Nicholas Singleton are locks.

Kalel Mullings , Julius Chestnut , and Michael Carter are competing for that fourth and presumed final spot at running back. Mullings has the benefit of being a sophomore draft pick who also plays special teams. He hasn't been healthy though, and Chestnut is beginning to capture momentum.

Chestnut leads all Titans running backs in rushing through two preseason games, and it's not particularly close. The former Sacred Heart standout has gained 95 yards via 13 attempts. He's averaging an impressive 7.31 yards per game, and ripped off a big 34-yard gain.

Chestnut has also added three receptions for 24 receiving yards to his offensive totals. He's consistently a preseason stud for the Titans. Nothing has changed this year, with Chestnut totally dominating the preseason again.

Chestnut is also an experienced special teams player. Some believe Mullings, a former college linebacker, has the edge on special teams. He may possess more upside on special teams, but coordinator John "Bones" Fassel trusts Chestnut, too.

Pollard and Spears will be the Titans' bellcows once regular-season football arrives. Chestnut could add depth and experience, though. He's a potential short-yardage back, and if the oft-injured Spears were to miss time, you'd like to think Chestnut is more trustworthy than the rookie Singleton, who is struggling in pass protection.

Chestnut is once again dominating the NFL preseason. The Titans have big-time roster decisions coming, with Carter, Mullings, and D'Ernest Johnson contending for Chestnut's roster spot.

articles.title: Kinley Rasmus breaks LLWS hits record for a girl, a day after notching her second strikeout record
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus continues to etch her name in the Little League World Series record book.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus continued her dominant run at the Little League World Series on Tuesday with another tournament record as her Phenix City, Alabama, team advanced from another elimination game.

A day after tying the total strikeouts records for a girl in the Little League World Series, Rasmus broke the tournament's record for most hits by a girl. She did so with a fifth-inning single that put runners on the corners in a 4-2 win for Phenix City over Tacoma, Washington.

The hit was Rasmus' fifth of the tournament to claim the record as her own. And Phenix City advanced while eliminating Tacoma.

On Monday, Rasmus made LLWS history on the mound — for the second time.

Rasmus struck out six to help lift Phenix City past West Chester, Pennsylvania, 6-5, in their elimination game Monday. The two-way star has compiled 14 total strikeouts in the tournament, which again matched Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts by a girl in tournament history.

Rasmus struck out eight in Phenix City's first game at the Little League World Series last week, which also tied a single-game record Davis set in 2014.

And thanks in part to Rasmus, Phenix City rallied out of a five-run hole on Monday night. Rasmus threw more than four scoreless innings after coming in for relief to help spark the rally. It marked the team's second straight elimination win.

Rasmus is the daughter of former MLB pitcher Cory Rasmus and the niece of former MLB outfielder Colby Rasmus . Cory is an assistant coach for Phenix City this summer, and both brothers played on Phenix City's 1999 Little League World Series team.

Rasmus is one of two girls playing in the tournament this year. Carsynn Meyer is playing for Paseo Verde (Nevada). They are among the 25 girls who have competed in the event's 79-year history.

While Phenix City can't lose again and advance, Rasmus has already put herself in elite LLWS company. She's one strikeout away from breaking Davis' record and may have another chance on the mound thanks to Tuesday's win.

Phenix City will next face Great Lakes winner Hamilton, Ohio, on Wednesday in another elimination game.
